Setting Value Where File format json-nested Settings → Files File mask locales/*.json Settings → Files Source template locales/en.json Settings → Files Source language en Settings → Basic Push branch weblate-translations Settings → Version control Merge style merge Settings → Version control Commit message templates chore(i18n): … Settings → Commit messages JSON indentation 2, spaces Settings → Files Sort JSON keys off Settings → Files Cleanup translation files enabled, project-wide Project → Add-ons Squash Git commits enabled, squash: all Operations → Add-ons Git export URL served natively — no add-on —

Merge style must stay merge. Weblate's default is rebase, which replays Weblate's own commits onto main on every pull. Because main allows only squash and rebase merges, those commits never become ancestors of main, so the replay repeats forever and eventually conflicts — see If the component gets stuck. With merge, Weblate merges main into its branch instead and a squashed upstream PR integrates cleanly.

json_indent replaced the "Customize JSON output" add-on, which Weblate removed in 5.13. Leave key sorting off — Weblate follows the en.json template order, and sorting would reshuffle every locale file into one unreviewable diff.

The Cleanup translation files add-on (weblate.cleanup.generic) removes keys no longer present in en.json. Without it, locale files accumulate stale keys. It is installed at project scope, not on the component, so it covers glossary too — which is why it does not appear in the component's own addons list.

The Squash Git commits add-on (weblate.git.squash) collapses a push into one commit instead of one per language. Enabled 2026-07-31 (#796) with squash: all and append_trailers: true. Before it, #734 arrived as twelve commits, and because main squash-merges they all landed in the merge commit body — cb8d9893 carries eleven * Translated using Weblate (…) bullets plus one * Update translation files.

It squashes the commits, not their messages: the add-on's own Commit message option is empty, so Weblate builds the body from the pending commits' messages and the single commit still repeats chore(i18n): update translations from Weblate once per language. Cosmetic — set that option if it ever bothers you.

weblate-translations is force-pushed and always was: Weblate's GitHub backend pushes with --force regardless of add-ons. Squashing rewrites more of the branch each time, so expect stale line comments on the long-lived translation PR and a git fetch --force for local checkouts. Not corruption.

There is no Git exporter add-on on this project. Hosted Weblate serves the component's repository at the git_export URL natively, so the recovery procedure's weblate remote needs nothing enabled.

Commit message templates use Conventional Commits, matching the rest of the repo. They had drifted from .weblate.yml and were corrected on the live component on 2026-07-31 (#796).

Auditing the configuration over the API

A plain GET on the component — no token needed — returns all 89 fields, including merge_style, push_branch, git_export and the message templates. wlc show returns only a trimmed subset, so use a raw request for an audit. squash_commits is not among the 89 — it is not a component field at all, which is why it never took effect while it sat in .weblate.yml.

Add-ons need a token, and are readable only in the right place. The /api/components/spieli/ui-strings/addons/ sub-path returns 405 Method Not Allowed for everyone; instead read the component's addons field, which holds /api/addons/<id>/ URLs, or list /api/addons/ for every add-on across scopes. Each object names its scope — component set and project null means component-level, and the reverse for project-wide.

Use a token for those two, or they will lie to you. Unauthenticated, /api/addons/ answers 200 with {"count": 0, "results": []} and /api/addons/<id>/ answers 404, so an audit without one concludes no add-ons are installed. wlc has no add-on subcommand, so changes stay a UI action.

ICU plural strings appear as a single field in the Weblate editor. Translators write the full ICU expression for their language.

Weblate cannot validate plural categories

Weblate's checks catch broken ICU syntax, but not a grammatically correct form placed in the wrong plural category. Nine Slovak strings shipped with the genitive plural in many — a category that, for Czech and Slovak, matches only fractional numbers — so every count from 5 upwards rendered ungrammatically (#747). The string parsed fine and Weblate reported no error.

translation-guide.md documents the per-language rule and how translators can verify it with Intl.PluralRules.

docs.title: Host a region for spieli.eu
docs.text:
spieli.eu is a public playground map. It holds no data of its own. Every region on it comes from a data-node that someone runs for that region. At the moment these are the German states, and we are looking for people to add more. A region does not have to be a whole country: a single state, district or city is just as welcome.

You can see which regions are already covered on the map itself, in the list of regions on spieli.eu, or in spieli.eu/registry.json. Even so, please come to #spieli:matrix.org before you start: someone may already be setting up your region, and we can help you choose its boundary.

An example of a well-mapped playground is Carl-Schurz-Straße in Fulda.

docs.title: What a data-node does
docs.text:
A data-node downloads the OpenStreetMap extract for your region, keeps the playground data and serves it over HTTPS. spieli.eu lists its address, and visitors' browsers load the playgrounds from your server while they look at your region. The data is read-only. There are no accounts, no cookies and nothing a visitor can write.

With automatic updates switched on, the data-node re-imports the data every 2 to 10 days and installs new spieli releases by itself.

docs.title: Your own map as well
docs.text:
The installer offers two modes, and both put your region on spieli.eu:

  • data-node runs only the database and the API.
  • data-node-ui also serves a playground map of your region on your own domain. Someone covering Austria could run it as my-playground-map.at. spieli.eu reads from the same API, so both maps show the same data.

Choose data-node-ui if you want a map you can point people to locally under its own name. When the installer then asks for the app mode, choose standalone.

docs.title: Server requirements
docs.text:
A small VPS is enough. A city-sized region uses about 100 MB of memory while serving and a large state up to about 550 MB; an import needs more, about 2 GB plus swap for a single region. Disk needs range from 0.2 GB for a city to about 4 GB for a large state, plus room for the import. Measured figures per region, and what to watch during an import: Sizing.

Once it runs, there is little to do: keep the server's operating system up to date and read the release notes now and then. If a release needs more than pulling the new images, its notes say so (see also Upgrading).

docs.title: Choosing a region
docs.text: A data-node covers one OpenStreetMap boundary relation. That can be a whole country, but a state, a district or a single city is fine too; other people can add the neighbouring regions later. spieli cuts it out of a Geofabrik extract that contains it. The measured figures go up to Bavaria, which has 13 million inhabitants. Larger countries work as well but need more memory and disk; please ask in the chat first.

docs.title: Setting it up
docs.text:
You need a Linux server with Docker and the Compose plugin, a domain or subdomain that points to it, and ports 80 and 443 open. The examples below use my-playground-map.at for a data-node covering Austria.

  1. Run the installer. The command for the current release is in the Quick Start, which also explains how to find your region's relation ID and extract. Choose data-node or data-node-ui, and answer yes to automatic updates.

  2. Set up HTTPS with the Traefik installer, which gets a certificate from Let's Encrypt: HTTPS setup. Choose mode 1, data-node-ui; the app's nginx then serves the API with the CORS headers spieli.eu needs. (The installer's data-node mode cannot reach the API at the moment, #1062; until that is fixed, install spieli as data-node-ui in step 1 too.)

  3. When the first import has finished, check the API from another machine. The answer should be 200 OK with the header Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, and playground_count should be above 0. With data-node-ui, your map is now at https://my-playground-map.at.

    curl -i https://my-playground-map.at/api/rpc/get_meta

  4. Send us the API address (https://my-playground-map.at/api), the name of the region and its country in #spieli:matrix.org, and we will add it to spieli.eu.

docs.title: Legal and privacy
docs.text:
The legal requirements depend on your country, and we cannot give legal advice. Two things to know:

  • If you set IMPRESSUM_NAME, IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS and IMPRESSUM_EMAIL in .env, spieli generates an imprint and a privacy notice. If you already have such pages, set IMPRESSUM_URL and PRIVACY_URL instead. spieli.eu links them from your region. In Germany a public service needs an imprint. How it works and what to restart after a change: Configure the instance → Legal pages.
  • For your privacy notice: visitors' browsers connect to your server, which therefore sees their IP address. By default nothing is logged or stored, and no cookies are set.

The data is © OpenStreetMap contributors and licensed under the ODbL. spieli.eu shows the attribution.

docs.title: Languages
docs.text: The map is available in German, English and Slovak. Other languages are being translated on Weblate, where help is welcome; a language appears in the map once it has been switched on in a release. A region in another language is still fine: the playground names come from OpenStreetMap as mapped.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Quick Start: installer, deployment scenarios, managing the stack
  • Scheduled Import: how automatic imports and updates work
  • Federation: how spieli.eu talks to data-nodes
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: The easiest way to deploy spieli is with the interactive installer. It downloads everything it needs, walks you through configuration, and optionally runs the first import.

docs.title: Which setup do you need?
docs.text:
You want to… Setup Go to Run a playground map for your region data-node-ui + standalone (the installer's defaults) this page Put your region on spieli.eu or another hub data-node or data-node-ui Host a Region for spieli.eu — the steps are the same for any hub Combine several regions on one map a hub: ui + hub, plus a registry.json Federated Deployment

All five combinations of deployment mode and app mode: Deployment modes. Why spieli is split this way: Federation: one map, many owners.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A Linux server with Docker and the Compose plugin, bash, openssl, and sha256sum (or shasum -a 256 on macOS). How much memory and disk a region needs: Sizing.
  • For a public instance: a domain or subdomain pointing to the server, and ports 80 and 443 open.
  • Your region's OSM relation ID and a Geofabrik extract that contains it (see below).

docs.title: Finding your region
docs.text:
OSM relation ID — search for your city, district or state on Nominatim or openstreetmap.org. The relation ID appears in the URL — e.g. openstreetmap.org/relation/62700 → ID is 62700.

PBF extract — browse download.geofabrik.de for an extract covering your region. It only needs to contain your region — a state extract works fine for a single district. The importer cuts your region out of it.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
TAG=v0.14.0  # check https://github.com/mfuhrmann/spieli/releases for the latest tag
curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mfuhrmann/spieli/releases/download/${TAG}/install.sh" -o install.sh
curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mfuhrmann/spieli/releases/download/${TAG}/install.sh.sha256" -o install.sh.sha256
sha256sum --check install.sh.sha256 && bash install.sh

docs.title: What the installer does
docs.text:
It checks that Docker, the Compose plugin and openssl are available, then asks, in this order:

  1. The deployment directory (default ./spieli).
  2. The deployment mode (data-node, ui or data-node-ui): which containers run. See Deployment modes.
  3. The app mode (standalone or hub): how the map behaves. Skipped for data-node.
  4. Depending on the mode: your region's OSM relation ID and Geofabrik PBF URL (if it has a database), the remote API_BASE_URL (remote frontend), or the registry URL and poll interval (hub).
  5. Optional links for the About dialog (a regional wiki page and a community chat), the map's start and minimum zoom, the radius for nearby places, the port, and the number of CPU threads for the import.
  6. Automatically keep data and software up to date? (recommended). Answering yes starts Watchtower, which installs new spieli releases by itself, and sets the importer to refresh the data every 2 to 10 days.
  7. Whether to set up imprint and privacy pages: let spieli generate them from your name and address, or link pages you already have. Either way, it asks for the instance's public URL.

Then it generates a database password, downloads compose.yml (and db/init.sql if the stack has a database), writes .env, creates registry.json for a hub, and offers to pull the images, start the stack and run the first import.

docs.title: Managing the stack
docs.text:
After setup, manage the stack from your deployment directory:

cd spieli

# Start the stack
docker compose --profile data-node-ui up -d

# Stop the stack
docker compose --profile data-node-ui down

Replace data-node-ui with whichever mode you chose at install time (DEPLOY_MODE in your .env). If you said yes to automatic updates, add --profile auto-update to both commands; otherwise Watchtower does not start with the rest.

To refresh the OSM data right now, see Refresh Data: with automatic updates, restarting the importer does not import early.

docs.title: Before you go public
docs.text:
The stack answers on plain HTTP (port 8080). Before you point people at it:

  1. HTTPS — spieli ships a Traefik stack that gets and renews a Let's Encrypt certificate: HTTPS setup.
  2. Imprint and privacy notice — required in Germany; spieli can generate both: Configure the instance → Legal pages.
  3. Security checklist — database password, exposed ports, headers: Security.
  4. Know when it breaks — Watching your instance.
  5. Updates — automatic or by hand: Upgrading.

Every setting with its default: Configuration Reference. Something not working: Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Adding a Data-node to an Existing Hub
docs.text:
This page is for operators who already have a running hub + data-node-ui setup on one host and want to add more regional backends without touching the existing stack.

If you are setting up from scratch, see Federated Deployment instead.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The hub is client-side: browsers fetch playground data directly from each data-node URL listed in registry.json. Every data-node must therefore be reachable over public HTTPS — a backend accessible only on localhost cannot be reached by a user's browser.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Existing hub + at least one data-node-ui running on the host.
  • A reverse proxy (Traefik or nginx) that can front additional backends on new ports or subdomains.
  • A public domain / subdomain for the new backend (e.g. berlin.example.com).
  • OSM relation ID and Geofabrik PBF URL for the new region — see Quick Start → Finding your region.

docs.title: Step 1 — Create the backend directory
docs.text:
Each backend is an independent Compose project in its own directory.

mkdir ~/spieli-berlin
cd ~/spieli-berlin
cp ~/spieli/compose.yml .   # copy from your existing deploy dir
cp -r ~/spieli/db .          # copy db/init.sql — required for DB initialisation

Why copy db/init.sql?

The PostgreSQL image runs every file in /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/ on first start. compose.yml bind-mounts ./db/init.sql into that directory. Without the file, Docker creates a directory at the mount target instead of a file, the init script silently fails, and PostgREST cannot connect.

docs.title: Step 2 — Write .env
docs.text:
COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=spieli-berlin   # unique per backend — avoids Docker name collisions
DEPLOY_MODE=data-node-ui
APP_PORT=8082                         # unique port — increment for each new backend
OSM_RELATION_ID=62422
PBF_URL=https://download.geofabrik.de/europe/germany/berlin-latest.osm.pbf
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<strong-random-password>
REIMPORT_INTERVAL_MIN_DAYS=1
REIMPORT_INTERVAL_MAX_DAYS=1

# Legal / Impressum (required under German law for public instances)
IMPRESSUM_NAME=Max Mustermann
IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS=Musterstraße 1, 12345 Berlin
IMPRESSUM_EMAIL=kontakt@example.com

Generate a strong password the way the installer does: openssl rand -hex 32. A hex password contains no characters that need escaping (see below).

Legal requirement (Germany)

Public instances in Germany require an Impressum. Set at minimum IMPRESSUM_NAME, IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS, and IMPRESSUM_EMAIL. The importer writes the generated HTML to api.legal_content and get_meta() exposes impressum_url / privacy_url so the Hub can surface legal links. Omitting these leaves the backend with has_legal: false in get_meta().

The legal text is written at the end of a full import only; an API_ONLY run does not rewrite it. After changing these values, run a one-shot import as in Refresh Data → Daemon mode.

Passwords with special characters

compose.yml puts the password into a PostgreSQL URI (postgres://osm:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/osm). Characters with a meaning in URIs (/, +, =, @, #), which openssl rand -base64 produces, break it, and PostgREST fails with could not look up local user ID. A hex password avoids this. If you must keep such a password, change PGRST_DB_URI in the postgrest service to the key-value form:

PGRST_DB_URI: "host=db port=5432 dbname=osm user=osm password=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"

docs.title: Step 3 — Start the stack
docs.text:
cd ~/spieli-berlin
docker compose --profile data-node-ui up -d

Do not add --profile auto-update

The Watchtower instance already running on this host (in the hub's stack) watches all containers on the Docker host. Adding a second Watchtower via --profile auto-update causes both instances to fight over the same containers, killing each other on startup.

docs.title: Step 4 — Import OSM data
docs.text:
The importer started automatically in Step 3 (daemon mode). Watch progress:

docker logs -f spieli-berlin-importer-1

Berlin (~93 MB PBF) takes a few minutes. The import is complete when you see [importer] Import completed successfully. The importer then sleeps until the next scheduled run.

docs.title: Verify playground count
docs.text:
curl -s https://berlin.example.com/api/rpc/get_meta | \
  python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['playground_count'], d['relation_id'])"

playground_count must be greater than zero. If it is 0, or name is missing or names the wrong region, see Troubleshooting → Map loads but shows no playgrounds (corrupt cache, wrong relation ID).

docs.title: Step 5 — Expose via reverse proxy
docs.text: The browser must reach the backend at a stable public HTTPS URL. If you use Traefik with the file provider (as set up by install-traefik.sh), drop a new file in the dynamic/ directory — Traefik picks it up immediately without a restart.

docs.title: Subdomain approach (recommended)
docs.text:
~/spieli-traefik/dynamic/berlin.yml:

http:
  routers:
    berlin:
      rule: "Host(`berlin.example.com`)"
      entryPoints:
        - websecure
      tls:
        certResolver: le
      service: berlin
      middlewares:
        - security-headers

  services:
    berlin:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - url: "http://host.docker.internal:8082"

security-headers is defined in your existing app.yml and is shared across all files in the same dynamic/ directory.

docs.title: Path-prefix approach (same domain)
docs.text:
Use this when you cannot add a new DNS subdomain.

~/spieli-traefik/dynamic/berlin.yml:

http:
  routers:
    berlin-api:
      rule: "Host(`your-domain.example.com`) && PathPrefix(`/berlin/api/`)"
      entryPoints:
        - websecure
      tls:
        certResolver: le
      service: berlin
      middlewares:
        - strip-berlin
        - security-headers

  middlewares:
    strip-berlin:
      stripPrefix:
        prefixes:
          - "/berlin"

  services:
    berlin:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - url: "http://host.docker.internal:8082"

With the path-prefix approach the registry URL must include the prefix: "url": "https://your-domain.example.com/berlin/api".

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
curl -i -H "Origin: https://your-hub-domain.example.com" \
  https://berlin.example.com/api/rpc/get_meta
# expect: 200 OK, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *

docs.title: Step 6 — Update registry.json and restart hub
docs.text:
Edit ~/spieli/registry.json (or wherever your hub's registry.json lives):

{
  "instances": [
    { "slug": "hessen", "url": "https://your-domain.example.com/api", "name": "Hessen" },
    { "slug": "berlin", "url": "https://berlin.example.com/api",      "name": "Berlin" }
  ]
}

The file is bind-mounted, so browsers see the new entry on their next page load. Restart the app container anyway: the Content Security Policy's connect-src is generated from this file at startup, and a new backend is missing from it until then.

cd ~/spieli
docker compose --profile ui restart app

docs.title: Verify end-to-end
docs.text: Open the hub in a browser. The instance pill should show the new region. If a backend appears red ("unreachable"), open DevTools → Network and check the get_meta request — the URL in the request must match the backend's actual public path.

docs.title: Port layout reference
docs.text:
Stack APP_PORT COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME Hub with its local data-node (e.g. Hessen) 8080 spieli Second data-node (e.g. Berlin) 8082 spieli-berlin Third data-node 8083 spieli-<region>

Keep ports consecutive and project names unique.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Federated Deployment — full from-scratch walkthrough
  • registry.json reference — schema and slug rules
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Backup and Restore
docs.text: Everything in the database can be regenerated from the OSM extract. What cannot be regenerated is your configuration.

docs.title: What to back up
docs.text:
Data Location Backup needed? OSM playground data pgdata Docker volume Optional — re-importable from PBF PBF cache pbf_cache Docker volume Optional — re-downloadable from Geofabrik Configuration .env file Yes — contains your passwords and settings Custom registry.json your deployment directory Yes (if Hub mode)

The most important thing to back up is your .env file. The database can always be rebuilt from the Geofabrik PBF (how long that takes). A lost .env means a lost POSTGRES_PASSWORD and requires recreating the stack from scratch.

docs.title: Back up the database
docs.text:
For a hot backup (database running):

docker compose exec db pg_dump -U osm osm | gzip > spieli-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).sql.gz

For a cold backup (database stopped), or to back up the raw volume:

docker compose --profile data-node-ui stop db

# Copy the volume to a compressed tar
docker run --rm \
  -v spieli_pgdata:/data \
  -v $(pwd):/backup \
  alpine tar czf /backup/pgdata-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz -C /data .

docker compose --profile data-node-ui start db

Replace spieli_pgdata with the actual volume name (docker volume ls to find it; typically <project-name>_pgdata).

docs.title: Restore the database
docs.text:
From a pg_dump backup:

# Stop the stack, recreate the DB volume, then restore
docker compose --profile data-node-ui down
docker volume rm spieli_pgdata       # ⚠️ destroys all data — only run if you have a backup!
docker compose --profile data-node-ui up -d db

# Wait for the DB to initialise (watch `docker compose logs -f db`)

# Restore
gunzip -c spieli-backup-20260501.sql.gz | docker compose exec -T db psql -U osm osm

# Apply the API schema (recreates PostgREST functions + materialised view).
# API_ONLY matters: without it this would be a full import that overwrites the restored data.
docker compose --profile data-node-ui run --rm -e API_ONLY=1 importer

# Restart the full stack
docker compose --profile data-node-ui up -d

docs.title: Re-import instead of restoring
docs.text:
Because the PBF is re-downloadable, a re-import is often simpler than a full restore:

docker compose --profile data-node-ui down
docker volume rm spieli_pgdata      # clear the database
docker compose --profile data-node-ui up -d

The import then starts as described in Refresh Data → After deleting the database.

The PBF files are stored in the pbf_cache volume and are reused automatically. If you deleted the volume too, the importer downloads a fresh copy (~300 MB for a state extract).

docs.title: Scheduled backups
docs.text:
To schedule daily backups with cron (adjust paths to your deployment):

0 3 * * * cd /opt/spieli && docker compose exec -T db pg_dump -U osm osm | gzip > /opt/backups/spieli-$(date +\%Y\%m\%d).sql.gz && find /opt/backups -name 'spieli-*.sql.gz' -mtime +14 -delete

This dumps the database at 3 AM and deletes backups older than 14 days.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Configuration reference — POSTGRES_PASSWORD and other variables to keep in your .env backup
  • Scheduled import — automating regular OSM data refreshes

docs.title: Basemap and external services
docs.text: The background map, search, photos and reviews come from third-party services. By default this instance fetches them itself and serves them from its own origin, so the visitor's browser contacts none of them. The defaults work without any setting; this page is for changing them. Every variable with its default: Configuration Reference. After a change, recreate the app container (Configure the instance → Applying changes).

docs.title: Basemap
docs.text: The basemap is requested on every map movement, so how it is delivered is a privacy decision as much as a rendering one. The reasoning behind the default is in Privacy by design; this section covers the settings.

docs.title: The default: a cached public tile server
docs.text:
Out of the box the bundled vector style references every asset under /basemap/ on this instance. nginx serves what is vendored in the image (the style document and the webfonts) from disk and fetches the rest — tiles and sprites — from BASEMAP_UPSTREAM, caching it.

Map labels are drawn from the vendored webfonts, not from the style's glyphs endpoint: ol-mapbox-style resolves text through a webfont CSS template rather than fetching glyph ranges. The style still declares glyphs under /basemap/, and that path proxies correctly if a future renderer does ask for it, but nothing requests it today. make basemap-fonts fails if the style asks for a font weight that is not vendored, because the alternative is a silent fallback to a system font plus an upstream request on every page load.

That arrangement does two jobs at once:

  • It is kind to the upstream. OpenFreeMap is donation-funded and run by one person. A federation of backends sending every visitor's tile requests straight there is not a neighbourly load pattern; a cache in front means one client per deployment, with duplicate misses collapsed (proxy_cache_lock) and conditional revalidation rather than full refetches.
  • Visitors' browsers never contact it. No third party sees a visitor's IP address or the z/x/y stream that reveals what they were looking at.

No request is written to the access log (#988, oci/app/00-no-access-log.conf). This covers the access log only. error_log still records the URI of a request that fails upstream, which is what keeps outages diagnosable; it is a record of failures rather than of browsing, but it is not nothing, so treat the container's error log with the same care as any other log that can name a path a visitor requested.

Without a volume the cache lives on the container's writable layer, and every rebuild or upgrade discards it, so the next visitors refill it from the upstream. That matters more here than for /tiles/: this cache is on by default, and an upgrade sweep across stacks would send every one of them cold at the public server. Both compose files mount a basemap_cache volume at /var/cache/nginx/basemap, so an installed stack keeps it.

Running several stacks on one host? Point them all at a single shared cache instead of running one per stack — see Shared Basemap Cache. Fifteen caches at the 4 GB default is up to 60 GB of disk and fifteen separate clients hitting the public tile server, all going cold together on every upgrade sweep.

To run your own tileserver, point BASEMAP_UPSTREAM at it (origin only, see below). If its URL layout differs from OpenFreeMap's, the bundled style also has to be rebuilt against it, which needs your own image: see Customise your own image → Your own tileserver.

BASEMAP_UPSTREAM must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]) with no path. A path is refused at startup rather than accepted, because proxy_pass with a variable replaces the request URI instead of prefixing it — every asset would collapse onto that one path and the map would render blank with no error.

docs.title: Two source shapes
docs.text:
Leave BASEMAP_STYLE_URL and BASEMAP_URL unset and you get the bundled vector style. The container serves /basemap/style.local.json and the make dev server falls back to /basemap/style.json; both are compiled-in defaults, not the env var's default — do not copy either into .env as a value. Setting BASEMAP_STYLE_URL marks the basemap as configured, which then requires BASEMAP_ATTRIBUTION — the container refuses to start without it. A style whose assets point at a third party is also rejected alongside BASEMAP_PROXY, since the style would bypass the proxy; the bundled style is same-origin and is accepted.

Precedence when you do set them:

Set Result neither the bundled vector style BASEMAP_STYLE_URL that style, vector BASEMAP_URL only that raster template — replaces the vector default entirely both the style renders; the raster URL is the fallback if the style fails to load

BASEMAP_URL is an OpenLayers XYZ raster template.

Raster templates are passed through verbatim, so a provider using a reversed axis order works without a code change:

BASEMAP_URL='https://sgx.geodatenzentrum.de/wmts_basemapde/tile/1.0.0/de_basemapde_web_raster_farbe/default/GLOBAL_WEBMERCATOR/{z}/{y}/{x}.png'

That example is included because it exercises the axis-order case, not as a recommendation: basemap.de covers Germany only, and outside Germany it returns 200 OK with a blank tile rather than an error. Nothing fails, nothing alerts, and a proxy cache will happily store the blanks. Check your provider's coverage against your region before adopting it.

Whatever you choose, make sure the credit matches. Showing one provider's attribution over another's tiles is a licence problem, not a cosmetic one.

For a vector basemap you normally do not have to do anything: a tile server declares its own attribution in its TileJSON, and the map uses that. It is authoritative and it differs between servers exactly as it should:

Upstream Credit shown tiles.openfreemap.org OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles Data from OpenStreetMap a self-hosted Planetiler build © OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributors

Setting BASEMAP_ATTRIBUTION overrides that. Only do so when you have a credit the server cannot know about, because an override that goes stale credits the wrong party silently — that is how a map built from self-hosted tiles came to display "© OpenFreeMap".

Note that this follows the tile server, not BASEMAP_UPSTREAM. With a shared cache the upstream is an internal host while the tiles still originate from the public server, so the hostname says nothing about who to credit.

A raster basemap has no TileJSON to ask, which is why BASEMAP_URL requires BASEMAP_ATTRIBUTION and the container refuses to start without it.

docs.title: Delivery modes
docs.text:
Mode Configuration Who sees the visitor cached (default) nothing — the bundled same-origin style Nobody. The browser talks only to this instance; tiles are fetched server-side from BASEMAP_UPSTREAM and cached direct BASEMAP_URL or BASEMAP_STYLE_URL pointing at a third party The provider receives every visitor's IP address, User-Agent, Referer and tile coordinates proxied BASEMAP_PROXY=true with a raster BASEMAP_URL The provider sees only this server. Predates the default above and applies to raster providers

A fourth mode, mirrored — shipping the tileset with the instance so no provider is contacted even server-side — is not implemented. A DE + CZ + SK PMTiles build is around 5 GB per stack, against a demand-driven cache that costs a fraction of that; BASEMAP_UPSTREAM is what makes the swap cheap if that changes.

Proxying has no fallback to direct delivery. If the upstream is unreachable, tiles fail and the map renders without a basemap. That is deliberate: falling back would leak exactly the addresses proxying was enabled to protect, at the moment something is already wrong.

For the same reason, enabling BASEMAP_PROXY alongside a vector style is rejected at startup whenever that style would still send the browser to a third party — the style takes precedence over the raster URL, so the browser would fetch everything directly while the proxy sat unused and the privacy page claimed otherwise.

That check looks at the style document, not just its URL. A same-origin BASEMAP_STYLE_URL proves nothing on its own: /basemap/style.json is served locally but points its tiles, glyphs and sprites at tiles.openfreemap.org, so it is rejected too. /basemap/style.local.json — the container default — is accepted, because its assets are all same-origin. Rebuild it with --asset-base first. Only a style whose assets are all same-origin can be combined with the proxy.

docs.title: Costs of proxying
docs.text:
Proxied tiles are served twice from the operator's point of view — inbound on a cache miss, outbound to every visitor always — so tile egress moves onto your server. Budget accordingly, and check that your chosen provider's terms permit proxying and caching; that is your responsibility, not spieli's.

The /tiles/ cache is not persistent by default. Without a volume it lives on the container's writable layer, so every rebuild or upgrade discards it and the next visitors refill it from the upstream. Mount a volume at /var/cache/nginx/tiles if you want it to survive rebuilds.

Invalid cache values fail at startup rather than being silently rewritten: 4.5g is rejected instead of quietly becoming 45g.

Two cache settings bind before disk does, and both have defaults that will surprise you:

  • BASEMAP_CACHE_KEYS_ZONE holds roughly 8000 keys per MB. The 10m seen in most nginx examples tracks about 80,000 tiles, so a large max_size behind it yields a cache that stays almost entirely empty.
  • BASEMAP_CACHE_INACTIVE defaults in nginx to 10 minutes, evicting tiles regardless of free space. spieli defaults it to 90 days instead.

Sizing depends heavily on raster versus vector. Vector tilesets cap at a low maximum zoom and the client renders deeper zooms by overzooming the same tiles, so full coverage is orders of magnitude smaller than the raster equivalent for the same area.

docs.title: Check your reverse proxy's log
docs.text: spieli writes no access log, including for proxied tiles (/tiles/). If you run a reverse proxy in front of it (Traefik, for example), check that it does not log the tile path either: at high zoom the z/x/y sequence is a record of what someone looked at, whichever layer writes it down.

docs.title: Regional tilesets
docs.text:
A tileset covering a few countries has two different extents, and only one of them is discoverable from the tileset itself.

Planetiler bakes Natural Earth and water polygons in globally, so low zooms render everywhere and the declared bounds describe that wide area honestly. OSM detail exists only inside the imported extract. Above roughly z7 outside it the tile server answers 204 No Content:

place z4 z6 z8 z10 z12 Fulda (covered) 200 200 200 200 200 Paris (outside) 200 200 204 204 204

The renderer draws an empty tile for a 204. Nothing errors and nothing warns, so the result is indistinguishable from a legitimately empty map.

BASEMAP_COVERAGE_BBOX closes that gap. Set it to where your detail actually is and the map shows a quiet notice once the view leaves it:

# Germany, Czechia and Slovakia
BASEMAP_COVERAGE_BBOX=5.8,47.2,22.6,55.1

Leave it unset for a planet tileset. Unset means the notice never appears, which is why this changes nothing for an existing deployment.

Two details worth knowing:

  • It keys on the view centre, not on the viewport overlapping the box. Near a border a partly-covered view is normal, and warning there would cry wolf.
  • It stays quiet below zoom 8, because the tileset's global low-zoom layer still renders there and nothing is actually missing.

A malformed value is ignored rather than fatal: a typo costs the notice, not the map.

docs.title: The bundled style
docs.text: make basemap-style builds the two vendored style files (style.json for make dev, style.local.json for the container) and decides what is changed against the upstream style. See Update Generated Assets → Basemap style.

docs.title: External-service proxies
docs.text:
By default the visitor's browser contacts no third party. Geocoding, playground photos and reviews are all fetched by this instance and served from its own origin, cached on disk. This is the same mechanism as the basemap, extended to the rest.

Browser ──► this instance ──► nginx cache ──► Nominatim / Commons / Mangrove

Each service can be opted out individually with the PROXY_* variables (Configuration Reference). Opting out restores direct browser requests for that service and adds its host to the generated Content Security Policy; the others stay proxied.

docs.title: One exception
docs.text:
Panoramax is not proxied at all. Its thumbnail endpoint answers 308 with a Location on a per-instance derivative host, and nginx cannot follow a redirect — relaying it would send the browser to a host the privacy page does not name and the CSP does not allow. Its viewer is an <iframe>, and serving a whole interactive third-party application from this origin would grant it same-origin privileges here. Both stay cross-origin, are named in the CSP, and keep their privacy-page rows.

Equipment illustrations used to be a second exception, because they were rendered from Special:FilePath redirects. Since #867 their file names are resolved at build time (make equipment-images), and the images are served through /ext/wikimedia/ like the photo gallery. See External Services → Equipment illustrations.

docs.title: Nothing is logged
docs.text:
Every proxy location sets access_log off; errors are still logged. Why that matters: Privacy by design → Nothing is written down.

If you put a reverse proxy in front of this stack, check that it is not logging the same paths a layer up. Traefik's access log is off by default; if you have enabled it, exclude /ext/.

docs.title: Nominatim needs its cache to survive restarts
docs.text:
The OSMF usage policy is an absolute 1 request per second. Proxying concentrates onto one IP the queries that used to spread across every visitor's, so the cache is load-bearing rather than an optimisation — and compose.yml mounts a named volume (ext_cache) for exactly that reason. A cache on the container's writable layer is discarded on every image rebuild, and an upgrade across a federation would send every instance cold at a 1 r/s upstream simultaneously.

The rate limiter sits on an internal loopback server rather than on the visitor-facing location, so only cache misses reach it. That placement matters: limit_req runs before the cache lookup, so on the visitor-facing location it sheds requests that were already cached — measured, two simultaneous visitors were enough to break search. When the limiter does shed, a stale cached answer is served if one is held.

The dominant query is shared: region-URL resolution such as /fulda is identical for every visitor of an instance, and it is what caches best.

docs.title: Sizing the cache
docs.text:
EXT_CACHE_MAX_SIZE defaults to a conservative 2 GB for all four services together. Commons image bytes dominate it. Raise it if du -sh on the volume sits at the ceiling and images are being re-fetched:

docker compose exec app du -sh /var/cache/nginx/ext

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
Every variable a stack reads from .env. The installer writes most of them; edit .env afterwards and recreate the affected containers (Configure the instance → Applying changes). How the settings fit together — language, memory, basemap, external services — is explained in Configure the instance.

Applies to names the container that reads the variable, which is also the one to recreate after a change; Compose means Docker Compose itself reads it. A variable for a container your DEPLOY_MODE does not start has no effect (Deployment modes).

docs.title: Role and region
docs.text: Variable Default Applies to Description DEPLOY_MODE — Compose Deployment mode: data-node, ui, or data-node-ui. Written by the installer. APP_MODE standalone app standalone (regional map) or hub (aggregation map). hub reads its backends from REGISTRY_URL; it runs with DEPLOY_MODE=ui, or with data-node-ui to serve one region of its own as well. See Federated Deployment. OSM_RELATION_ID 62700 app, importer OSM relation ID of the region to display PBF_URL Hessen extract importer Geofabrik .osm.pbf download URL API_BASE_URL /api app Base URL of the PostgREST API. Set to the remote URL for ui mode (e.g. https://data.example.com/api). APP_PORT 8080 Compose Host port the app is exposed on POSTGRES_PASSWORD CHANGE_ME (installed stack), change-me (source) db, importer, PostgREST Database password. The installer generates a random one (openssl rand -hex 32); change it if you set the stack up by hand. Hex avoids characters that break the connection URI

docs.title: Map and interface
docs.text: Variable Default Applies to Description APP_NAME spieli app Name of the installed app (Chrome/Edge "Install app", Safari "Add to Dock", iOS "Add to Home Screen") — what the Dock, start menu and home screen show. Each stack installs as its own app, so give each region its own, e.g. spieli Fulda. Written into /manifest.webmanifest at container start. DEFAULT_LOCALE (browser) app UI language. Leave empty to auto-detect from the visitor's browser. Supported: de, en, sk. An unsupported value falls back to en. REGION_LANG de app Language your region's playgrounds are named in (BCP 47). Not the same as DEFAULT_LOCALE — see Language settings. REGION_COUNTRY de app Country whose public-holiday calendar opening_hours values are evaluated against (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). REGION_STATE (unset) app State for holiday calendars that vary by state: the ISO 3166-2 code (he or DE-HE) or the state's name (Hessen, Thüringen; letter case does not matter). Leave empty to keep the library default. Must be a state the opening_hours library has holidays for; anything else is ignored with a console warning. MAP_ZOOM 12 app Initial map zoom level. The installer writes 12 (standalone) or 6 (hub) MAP_MIN_ZOOM 10 app Minimum zoom level. The installer writes 7 (standalone) or 4 (hub) POI_RADIUS_M 5000 app Radius in metres for nearby POI search REGION_PLAYGROUND_WIKI_URL Generic OSM wiki app Wiki page linked in the "Contribute data" modal REGION_CHAT_URL (hidden) app Community chat link shown in the "Contribute data" modal; leave empty to hide the button. In hub mode this is the hub operator's own channel — backends do not contribute one.

docs.title: Basemap
docs.text: Variable Default Applies to Description BASEMAP_UPSTREAM https://tiles.openfreemap.org app Where the bundled style's tiles and sprites are fetched from and cached. Origin only (scheme://host[:port]), no path. Point it at your own tileserver to stop using a public one — a two-step swap, see Basemap. BASEMAP_URL (unset) app Raster basemap as an OpenLayers XYZ template. Placeholders are substituted by name, so a provider using {z}/{y}/{x} needs no code change. See Basemap. BASEMAP_STYLE_URL (unset — the app falls back to /basemap/style.json) app MapLibre style document, rendered as vector tiles. Takes precedence over BASEMAP_URL. See Basemap. BASEMAP_COVERAGE_BBOX (unset — no limit) app minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat where the basemap has detailed data. Only needed for a regional tileset; unset is correct for a planet one. See Regional tilesets. BASEMAP_ATTRIBUTION (the tile server's own credit) app Overrides the attribution the map shows. Leave unset and the credit comes from the tile server itself, which is correct for any upstream. Required whenever BASEMAP_URL or BASEMAP_STYLE_URL is set — the container refuses to start otherwise. Trusted HTML: rendered into the page as-is. BASEMAP_PROXY (unset) app true serves tiles through this instance, so the browser fetches from same-origin /tiles/ and never contacts the provider. The upstream origin and the tile path are derived from BASEMAP_URL. See Basemap. BASEMAP_CACHE_MAX_SIZE 4g app Disk ceiling per cache zone. The basemap cache always exists; enabling BASEMAP_PROXY adds a second zone sized from the same value, so the on-disk total can be twice this. BASEMAP_CACHE_KEYS_ZONE 64m app nginx cache key zone. Holds roughly 8000 keys per MB and binds before disk does — a large BASEMAP_CACHE_MAX_SIZE behind a small keys zone yields a cache that stays almost empty. BASEMAP_CACHE_INACTIVE 90d app How long an unrequested tile survives. nginx defaults to 10 minutes, which evicts tiles regardless of free space — far too short for basemap tiles.

docs.title: External services and CSP
docs.text: Variable Default Applies to Description PROXY_NOMINATIM true app Fetch geocoding server-side through /ext/nominatim/ so the browser never contacts Nominatim. false restores direct browser requests. See External-service proxies. PROXY_COMMONS true app Fetch the Commons API and the image bytes server-side (/ext/commons/, /ext/wikimedia/). PROXY_MANGROVE true app Fetch and submit reviews server-side through /ext/mangrove/. Submission still verifies at Mangrove: the JWT signature covers its own claims, so the proxy is transparent to it. OSM_NOTES_URL (empty — the public OSM API) app Where "Missing a playground?" hints go as anonymous OSM notes (#1000). An https:// origin with no path. false turns the anonymous hint off; the MapComplete option stays. Not proxied: the browser sends the note itself, only when the visitor presses Send, and the host is added to the generated CSP and privacy page. For testing, use the OSM dev sandbox https://master.apis.dev.openstreetmap.org so no real notes are created. EXT_CACHE_MAX_SIZE 2g app Disk ceiling for the shared /ext/ cache. One zone serves all four services; the default cache key includes the upstream host, so two upstreams cannot collide on a path. EXT_CACHE_KEYS_ZONE 16m app Key zone for the /ext/ cache. Same caveat as the basemap one: it binds before disk does. EXT_CACHE_INACTIVE 30d app How long an unrequested /ext/ response survives. CSP_CONNECT_EXTRA (unset) app Extra origins for the generated connect-src, space-separated. Needed when a hub fetches registry.json from a URL at runtime, so the entrypoint cannot read it to discover backends. Rejected at startup if malformed. See Content Security Policy. CSP_IMG_EXTRA (unset) app Extra origins for the generated img-src, space-separated. Needed when images are rendered from an origin the generator cannot discover. Rejected at startup if malformed.

docs.title: Import and schedule
docs.text: Variable Default Applies to Description OSM2PGSQL_THREADS 4 importer CPU threads for the osm2pgsql data-loading step REIMPORT_INTERVAL_MIN_DAYS (unset) importer Minimum days between automatic OSM re-imports (daemon mode). Leave unset to run one-shot (import once and exit). Must be set together with REIMPORT_INTERVAL_MAX_DAYS. REIMPORT_INTERVAL_MAX_DAYS (unset) importer Maximum days between automatic OSM re-imports. The importer picks a random interval in [MIN, MAX] days after each successful run. Recommended: 2–10. Must be set together with REIMPORT_INTERVAL_MIN_DAYS. REIMPORT_JITTER_HOURS 6 importer Daemon mode: a random 0–N hours added to every scheduled wait, and before an import that is already overdue at startup, so stacks that once imported together (after an upgrade sweep or reboot) drift apart instead of sharing a slot (#882). An overdue import is never held back past MAX_DAYS + this window. 0 disables it; with MIN == MAX the importer then warns. Not a whole number → default, with a log warning. REIMPORT_STARTUP_JITTER_MAX_HOURS 0 importer On a fresh DB (no prior import recorded), sleep a random duration between 0 and this many hours before the first import. Prevents a thundering herd when many backends are deployed simultaneously. Has no effect on restarts or routine cycles (that is REIMPORT_JITTER_HOURS). Recommended value for multi-backend deployments: 6. Before #882 compose did not pass it to the importer, so a value in .env had no effect. OSM_BBOX (auto) importer Manual bounding box for the osmium pre-filter (west,south,east,north). Skips Nominatim lookup when set. OSM_BBOX_PADDING 0.15 importer Degrees of padding added to each side of the Nominatim bbox (≈ 15 km). OSM_PREFILTER_MIN_MB 20 importer Source PBF files smaller than this many MB skip the osmium pre-filter step.

docs.title: Database tuning
docs.text: Variable Default Applies to Description PG_MAX_PARALLEL_WORKERS 2 importer Total parallel worker processes available to PostgreSQL (set ≤ CPU count). Persisted via ALTER SYSTEM in api.sql. PG_MAX_PARALLEL_WORKERS_PER_GATHER 2 importer Parallel workers per query. Must be ≤ PG_MAX_PARALLEL_WORKERS. PG_MAX_PARALLEL_MAINTENANCE_WORKERS 2 importer Parallel workers for CREATE INDEX / VACUUM. Must be ≤ PG_MAX_PARALLEL_WORKERS. PG_MAINTENANCE_WORK_MEM 256MB importer Memory per maintenance operation (index builds etc.). Total peak ≈ value × (PG_MAX_PARALLEL_MAINTENANCE_WORKERS + 1). Must include a unit suffix (kB, MB, GB, TB); a bare integer is interpreted as kilobytes by PostgreSQL. PG_WORK_MEM 32MB importer Memory per sort/hash operation inside parallel workers. Total peak per query ≈ value × (PG_MAX_PARALLEL_WORKERS_PER_GATHER + 1) × hash/sort nodes. Must include a unit suffix (kB, MB, GB, TB); a bare integer is interpreted as kilobytes by PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Hub
docs.text: Variable Default Applies to Description REGISTRY_URL /registry.json app URL of the registry JSON listing backends. Default is same-origin; bind-mount or bake in a custom file. See Federated Deployment and registry.json reference. HUB_POLL_INTERVAL 300 app Seconds between the hub's refreshes of each backend's get_meta (counts, data age, health) and of /federation-status.json. The registry itself is read once per page load. Bare integer, no unit suffix. MACRO_MAX_ZOOM 7 app Maximum zoom level at which the macro view (one summary ring per backend) is shown instead of individual cluster circles. Increase for deployments with many backends covering a small geographic area; decrease for sparse deployments covering a large area. CLUSTER_MAX_ZOOM 13 app Highest zoom level at which playgrounds are drawn as clusters; above it, each playground is drawn on its own. Standalone and hub alike.

docs.title: Legal pages
docs.text: Variable Default Applies to Description SITE_URL (unset) app, importer Public base URL of this instance (e.g. https://spieli.example.com). Used to construct absolute impressum_url and privacy_url in get_meta() so the Hub can discover legal pages without an operator-supplied override URL. get_meta() emits the legacy paths SITE_URL + /impressum and + /datenschutz, which the app permanently redirects to the canonical /legal/impressum and /legal/datenschutz. Leave unset for purely local testing. IMPRESSUM_NAME (unset) app, importer Full name of the legally responsible person or organisation. Required to generate the Impressum (with IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS) and the Datenschutz page (with IMPRESSUM_EMAIL). On a data-node the importer also stores the generated text for the hub. IMPRESSUM_ORG (unset) app, importer Organisation name (if different from IMPRESSUM_NAME). Optional; omitted from the Impressum when empty. IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS (unset) app, importer Street address and city (e.g. Musterstraße 1, 36037 Fulda). Required alongside IMPRESSUM_NAME. IMPRESSUM_EMAIL (unset) app, importer Contact email address. Required for the Datenschutz page; shown on the Impressum when set. IMPRESSUM_PHONE (unset) app, importer Contact phone number. Optional; omitted from the Impressum when empty. IMPRESSUM_URL (unset) app, importer Override URL for an existing Impressum page (e.g. https://example.com/impressum). When set, the generated impressum.html is skipped and this URL is used directly in get_meta() and config.js. PRIVACY_URL (unset) app, importer Override URL for an existing Datenschutzerklärung page. When set, the generated datenschutz.html is skipped.

docs.title: Compose profiles
docs.text: Which containers each DEPLOY_MODE starts, and the auto-update profile: Deployment modes → Compose profiles.

docs.title: Configure the instance
docs.text: How the settings in .env work together, for the areas where that takes more than one line. Every variable, with its default, is listed in the Configuration Reference.

docs.title: Applying changes
docs.text:
After editing .env, restart the relevant containers. Replace <mode> with your DEPLOY_MODE value (data-node, ui, or data-node-ui):

# Restart app only (config changes)
docker compose --profile <mode> up -d app

# Full restart
docker compose --profile <mode> down
docker compose --profile <mode> up -d

Changing the legal settings needs more than an app restart: see Legal pages → Applying changes.

docs.title: Legal pages
docs.text:
In Germany a public service needs an imprint (Impressum) and a privacy notice (Datenschutzerklärung); other countries have their own rules. We cannot give legal advice. What spieli does for you: the installer asks for the details (or lets you skip them), and the settings below decide what is generated.

Option 1: let spieli generate the pages. Set the contact details in .env:

Page Served at Needs Imprint /legal/impressum IMPRESSUM_NAME and IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS; IMPRESSUM_ORG, IMPRESSUM_EMAIL, IMPRESSUM_PHONE appear when set Privacy notice /legal/datenschutz IMPRESSUM_NAME and IMPRESSUM_EMAIL

The app container writes both pages at startup, in German. Without the required values a page still exists but says that the operator's details have not been configured yet. The privacy notice is generated from the actual configuration: which external services the visitor's browser contacts, and which only your server does, follows the PROXY_* and basemap settings (Basemap and external services), so it does not need editing by hand when those change.

Option 2: link pages you already have. Set IMPRESSUM_URL and PRIVACY_URL. The corresponding page is then not generated, and the app links your URL instead.

SITE_URL (for example https://spieli.example.com) should be set whenever the instance is public. A hub links your legal pages from absolute URLs, which get_meta() builds from SITE_URL unless IMPRESSUM_URL / PRIVACY_URL give them directly; with neither, the hub gets no URL.

What a hub shows for your region. In its region list a hub links the URLs from your get_meta(). On a data-node the importer also stores the generated imprint and privacy text in the database (when IMPRESSUM_NAME and IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS are set), so a hub can show it even when no URL is available.

docs.title: Applying legal changes
docs.text:
After changing IMPRESSUM_*, SITE_URL, IMPRESSUM_URL or PRIVACY_URL, three things are refreshed separately:

  1. This instance's own pages: recreate the app container (restart would keep the old environment): 
    docker compose --profile <mode> up -d app
  2. The links a hub shows come from get_meta(), which bakes the URLs in when api.sql is applied. Recreate the daemon importer (up -d importer: it applies a changed api.sql on startup), or run docker compose --profile <mode> run --rm -e API_ONLY=1 importer.
  3. The legal text a hub shows for a data-node is rewritten only at the end of a full import. See Refresh Data.

docs.title: Language settings
docs.text:
DEFAULT_LOCALE and REGION_LANG answer different questions and are deliberately independent:

Question Affects DEFAULT_LOCALE What language is the interface in? Every translated label, and the document's lang attribute REGION_LANG What language are the playgrounds named in? The lang attribute on OSM-derived names

A Fulda instance serving an English-speaking audience sets DEFAULT_LOCALE=en and keeps REGION_LANG=de: the buttons read "Filter", but the playgrounds are still called Spielplatz Am Rosengarten. Screen readers use these attributes to pick a pronunciation, and CSS hyphenation uses REGION_LANG to break long compound names correctly.

Set REGION_LANG to the language your OSM name tags are actually written in. A bilingual region gets one value for all names — per-object language is not derivable from OSM data.

REGION_COUNTRY and REGION_STATE are separate again: they only affect how public holidays in opening_hours values are resolved. A German-language deployment serving Austrian playgrounds sets REGION_LANG=de with REGION_COUNTRY=at.

Only opening_hours values with PH (public holiday) are affected — 69 of 7 042 playgrounds in the Hessen extract (September 2026). A value the app cannot resolve is ignored and logged in the browser console as [config] REGION_STATE "…" is not a state of …, listing the codes it knows.

A state code such as he and a state name such as Hessen both work; with either, a playground tagged PH off shows as closed on that state's holidays, for example Corpus Christi in Hessen.

docs.title: RAM sizing
docs.text:
How PG_* values are applied. The importer runs ALTER SYSTEM SET … at the top of api.sql, then SELECT pg_reload_conf(). The values are persisted to postgresql.auto.conf inside the data volume and apply to every connection — including PostgREST — without restarting the database container. To re-tune, edit .env and re-apply the schema only: 

docker compose --profile <mode> run --rm -e API_ONLY=1 importer
Without API_ONLY=1 this runs a full import — or, on a stack with automatic updates, starts a second importer daemon next to the running one.

Stacks installed from an older release

Until the release that fixed #1060, the compose files passed higher values (6 / 4 / 4 · 512MB · 128MB, a peak of about 3 GB), and they win whenever .env does not set the variables. A stack keeps its compose.yml across upgrades, so it keeps those values until you fetch the new compose.yml (Upgrading → requires-compose-update) or set the values from the table below in .env.

Defaults are sized for a 2-core / 4 GB host (peak ≈ 1.5 GB during the heaviest single operation, CREATE INDEX). Recommended values per host size:

Host RAM / cores WORKERS / PER_GATHER / MAINT MAINT_WORK_MEM WORK_MEM Approx. peak 4 GB / 2 core (default) 2 / 2 / 2 256MB 32MB ~1.5 GB 8 GB / 4–6 core 4 / 2 / 4 512MB 64MB ~3 GB 16 GB / 8 core 8 / 4 / 4 1GB 128MB ~6 GB

The driver of the peak is CREATE INDEX parallelism (≈ MAINT_WORK_MEM × (MAINT_WORKERS + 1)) followed by the materialised view rebuild (≈ WORK_MEM × (PER_GATHER + 1) × ~4 hash/sort nodes). These run sequentially, so the budget is the larger of the two plus baseline (~700 MB for shared_buffers default + PostgREST pool + WAL + autovacuum).

docs.title: Scheduling OSM re-imports
docs.text: Two ways, both described in Scheduled Import: daemon mode (set REIMPORT_INTERVAL_MIN_DAYS and REIMPORT_INTERVAL_MAX_DAYS; the installer does this when you choose automatic updates) or a one-shot importer started by a systemd timer or cron.

docs.title: Basemap and external services
docs.text: Where the background map comes from, and how search, photos and reviews are fetched without the visitor's browser contacting a third party: Basemap and external services. The defaults need no setting.

docs.title: Customise your own image
docs.text: Everything in Configuration is a setting in .env. This page is for the few changes that go further and need your own build of the app image: a different basemap style, a registry.json inside the image, a narrower CORS policy, error reporting. You stay an operator; you just build the image yourself instead of pulling it.

docs.title: Building the image
docs.text:
Check out the release you run, make your change, and build from the repository root:

git clone https://github.com/mfuhrmann/spieli.git
cd spieli
git checkout vX.Y.Z          # the release you run
# … your change …
docker build -f oci/app/Dockerfile -t my-spieli:vX.Y.Z .

Then point the app service in your installed compose.yml at it (image: my-spieli:vX.Y.Z) and recreate it with docker compose --profile <mode> up -d app. Two things follow from running your own image:

  • Watchtower cannot update it. It only follows published images. Repeat the build for every release, on top of the new tag.
  • Keep the change small, so it rebases cleanly onto the next release.

docs.title: Your own tileserver
docs.text:
BASEMAP_UPSTREAM in .env switches the cache to another tileserver. That alone is enough if the server mirrors OpenFreeMap's URL layout. The bundled style carries the provider's asset paths (/planet, /sprites/ofm_f384/ofm), and the cache only swaps the origin in front of them, so a differently laid-out server needs the style rebuilt against it, in your own image:

# in your checkout: rebuild the style against the new provider
tools/build-basemap-style.py --source https://my-tileserver/styles/foo \
                             --asset-base /basemap \
                             --out app/public/basemap/style.local.json
# build the image as above, then in the stack's .env (origin only — a path is rejected at startup):
BASEMAP_UPSTREAM=http://tileserver:8080

docs.title: A built-in registry.json
docs.text: For a hub, instead of bind-mounting the file (Federated Deployment → Replace the bundled registry.json): put your registry.json at app/public/registry.json in your checkout before building. No compose.override.yml is needed then, but every change to the list means a rebuild.

docs.title: Restrict CORS
docs.text:
Data-nodes answer /api/ with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on purpose: every hub's visitors must be able to read them. To allow only specific hub origins, edit the add_header Access-Control-Allow-Origin lines in oci/app/nginx.conf before building your image.

Any hub you leave out can no longer show your region.

docs.title: Frontend error reporting
docs.text:
spieli ships no frontend error reporting, and adding one is a source change rather than a setting:

  • The Content Security Policy allows scripts from the instance's own origin only (script-src 'self'), so an SDK loaded from a CDN or injected through nginx or config.js is blocked. It has to be bundled into the app build.
  • The reporting endpoint must be added to CSP_CONNECT_EXTRA, or the narrowed policy (report-only today, enforced later) blocks the reports.
  • Error reports carry visitor data (IP address, browser, the page) to a third party. Name the service on the privacy page; spieli's generated privacy page does not know about it.

docs.title: The map renders, but labels or icons are missing
docs.text:
Symptom: the basemap draws roads, water and landcover, but place names are missing, or they render in a system font that looks wrong next to the rest of the UI.

Cause: the webfonts the style asks for are not vendored in the image. Labels are drawn from /basemap/fonts/<family>/<weight>.css, not from the style's glyphs endpoint, and a missing weight fails silently: the renderer falls back to a system font and the map still renders. It also puts a request the tile server cannot answer on every page load.

Fix: check which weights the style asks for and re-vendor them.

# Lists the style's font stacks and fails if one has no vendored file
make basemap-fonts
# What is actually in the image:
docker compose exec app ls /usr/share/nginx/html/basemap/fonts/noto-sans/

Noto Sans Bold needs 700.css, Noto Sans Italic needs 400-italic.css, and so on. make basemap-fonts fetches all of them and then asserts the coverage, so a green run means every stack in the style resolves.

Missing icons rather than labels point at the sprite sheet instead: check that /basemap/sprites/… returns 200 and not 404.

curl -sI http://localhost:8080/basemap/sprites/ofm_f384/ofm.png | head -1

A 404 there usually means an nginx location-precedence problem — regex locations are matched before plain prefixes, so a ~* \.png$ block can claim these paths unless the /basemap/ location uses ^~.

docs.title: Container refuses to start: style.local.json is missing from the image
docs.text:
Symptom: the app container exits immediately with

[spieli] FATAL: app/public/basemap/style.local.json is missing from the image.

Cause: style.local.json is generated by make basemap-style and committed; your checkout does not have it (deleted, or a build from a modified tree). The check is deliberate: the entrypoint refuses to fall back to style.json, whose assets point at the public tile server, because that would silently send every visitor to a third party while the docs promise the opposite.

Fix: regenerate both style variants and rebuild.

make basemap-style     # writes style.json and style.local.json from one fetch
docker build -f oci/app/Dockerfile -t my-spieli:vX.Y.Z .

docs.title: Federated Deployment (Hub + data-nodes)
docs.text:
A federated deployment consists of one Hub UI (no local database) aggregating two or more regional data-nodes into a single map. Users browse at the Hub's URL; their browser talks directly to each data-node's PostgREST /api/, merging the results client-side.

This walkthrough stands up the topology end-to-end. For a single-region deployment, see the Quick Start instead.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    browser["Browser"]
    hub["Hub UI<br/>DEPLOY_MODE=ui, APP_MODE=hub<br/>serves the app and registry.json<br/>no database, no /api/"]
    a["Data-node A<br/>DEPLOY_MODE=data-node-ui<br/>PostGIS + PostgREST<br/>nginx serves /api/ with CORS"]
    b["Data-node B<br/>DEPLOY_MODE=data-node-ui<br/>PostGIS + PostgREST<br/>nginx serves /api/ with CORS"]

    browser -- "app + registry.json" --> hub
    browser -- "/api/ (cross-origin)" --> a
    browser -- "/api/ (cross-origin)" --> b

Each data-node runs the full data-node-ui profile so the shipped nginx config serves /api/ with the CORS headers the Hub's browser clients need. The Hub is the same frontend image flipped to APP_MODE=hub with a registry.json listing the data-node API URLs, and no database of its own.

Pure DEPLOY_MODE=data-node (advanced)

The data-node profile (invoked with --profile data-node) ships db + PostgREST only — no HTTP server, no port publish, no CORS handling. You can use it if you run your own reverse proxy in front of the PostgREST container and add the right Access-Control-Allow-* headers to /api/ responses. In the usual setup, use data-node-ui — it is what this walkthrough assumes. In data-node-ui mode only /api/ needs to be reachable from the Hub's origin; front the APP_PORT with a reverse proxy that blocks paths other than /api/ if you don't want the secondary standalone UI publicly reachable.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• One host (or cluster) per node — the Hub and each data-node can run on the same machine or on separate ones. Each must reach the others over HTTP/HTTPS.
  • Docker with the Compose plugin on every host.
  • One OSM relation ID and one Geofabrik PBF URL per data-node (how to find them).
  • HTTPS-terminating reverse proxy in front of each data-node in production — the browser must be able to fetch the data-node's /api/ over HTTPS when the Hub itself is served over HTTPS.
  • When co-locating nodes on one host, give each its own APP_PORT (e.g. 8080, 8081, 8082) and its own COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME (e.g. spieli-fulda, spieli-neuhof, spieli-hub) so port bindings and Docker resource names don't collide.
  • Data-node version: each data-node must run a release that ships the tiered playground API (get_playground_clusters, get_playgrounds_bbox, get_playground) and the completeness fields on get_meta (complete, partial, missing). These exist since v0.4.9; an older data-node still joins successfully but degrades to a legacy fallback path — see the federation reference's Federation endpoints table for the degradation matrix. If you can, upgrade every data-node before pointing a current Hub at it.

docs.title: Step 1 — Stand up each data-node
docs.text: Repeat on every data-node host. For this walkthrough the two backends are "Fulda" and "Neuhof".

docs.title: Data-node .env
docs.text:
Replace <strong-random-password> with an actual generated secret (openssl rand -hex 32; base64 characters such as /, + and = break the database connection URI) — the angle brackets are a placeholder, not a literal value.

DEPLOY_MODE=data-node-ui
OSM_RELATION_ID=454863
PBF_URL=https://download.geofabrik.de/europe/germany/hessen-latest.osm.pbf
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<strong-random-password>

No APP_MODE, no REGISTRY_URL — the frontend on a data-node runs in its default standalone mode purely so nginx can serve /api/ with CORS. API_BASE_URL stays at its default /api.

docs.title: Start the backend and import
docs.text:
docker compose --profile data-node-ui up -d
docker compose --profile data-node-ui run --rm importer

The first command starts db, postgrest, and the app container (which hosts nginx in front of PostgREST). The second runs the importer once — see Sizing → Import duration for timings, and Import Pipeline for what it does.

docs.title: Expose /api/ to the Hub
docs.text:
Because the Hub's browser clients hit /api/ cross-origin, each data-node must be reachable at a stable URL (e.g. https://fulda.example.com/api) and respond with CORS headers. The shipped nginx config in data-node-ui mode adds Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and the right methods on /api/ automatically — no extra configuration needed. In production, front APP_PORT with an HTTPS-terminating reverse proxy.

Verify from a machine that is not the data-node itself:

curl -i https://fulda.example.com/api/rpc/get_meta
# expect 200 OK, JSON body with { relation_id, name, playground_count, bbox }
# response should also include: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *

docs.title: Step 2 — Prepare registry.json
docs.text:
The Hub discovers its data-nodes by fetching a registry.json from its own origin. Create the file you'll deploy with the Hub:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "slug": "fulda",
      "url":  "https://fulda.example.com/api",
      "name": "Fulda"
    },
    {
      "slug": "neuhof",
      "url":  "https://neuhof.example.com/api",
      "name": "Neuhof"
    }
  ]
}

Every entry needs a url; set a name (otherwise the URL is shown) and a slug for stable deep links. Field rules, slug validation and the fields the hub fills in itself: registry.json reference.

The file is served from the Hub's own origin under /registry.json (the default value of REGISTRY_URL). It is not fetched from one of the data-nodes. CORS is not needed for the registry file itself, only for the data-node APIs it points at (handled in Step 1).

docs.title: Hub .env
docs.text:
DEPLOY_MODE=ui
APP_MODE=hub
REGISTRY_URL=/registry.json
HUB_POLL_INTERVAL=300
APP_PORT=8080

Notes:

  • REGISTRY_URL=/registry.json is the default and means "same origin as the Hub". Set a different value only if you host the registry elsewhere. The value is sanitized by the container entrypoint — only A-Z a-z 0-9 : / . + _ % ~ ? # & = @ , ; - survive, so query strings (?v=2) and fragments (#anchor) are preserved, but quotes, backslashes, angle brackets, $, backticks, parentheses and whitespace are dropped. Percent-encode anything outside that set.
  • HUB_POLL_INTERVAL is seconds as a bare integer (e.g. 300, not 300s). Every 300 seconds by default, each open browser re-reads every data-node's get_meta (counts, bounding box, data age). Playground data itself is fetched as the map moves, not on this timer.
  • API_BASE_URL is deliberately absent on a Hub. The Hub speaks to multiple data-nodes over CORS and reads their URLs from registry.json; a single API_BASE_URL would be meaningless.
  • OSM_RELATION_ID, PBF_URL, POSTGRES_PASSWORD are not set on the Hub — it has no database.

docs.title: Replace the bundled registry.json (required)
docs.text:
The Hub's shipped image bundles a development registry.json pointing at /api and /api2. Those paths have no upstream in the ui profile, so a Hub started without this step will load with every backend marked red.

If you set the Hub up with the installer and kept REGISTRY_URL=/registry.json, this is already done: it writes registry.json next to compose.yml and enables the bind-mount below. Otherwise pick one of the following — neither is optional:

Option A — bind-mount via compose.override.yml (recommended, no rebuild)

Create compose.override.yml alongside compose.yml:

services:
  app:
    volumes:
      - ./registry.json:/usr/share/nginx/html/registry.json:ro

Docker Compose merges this file automatically — no extra -f flags needed, and it survives future compose.yml upgrades.

Option B — custom image

Bake your registry.json into your own image; see Customise your own image → A built-in registry.json.

docs.title: Start the Hub
docs.text:
docker compose --profile ui up -d

No rebuild required; nginx serves the file immediately.

The Hub has no importer, no database, no run --rm importer step.

docs.title: Step 4 — Verify
docs.text:
1. Open the Hub URL in a browser (e.g. https://hub.example.com).
  2. You should see the map render, fit to the union of all configured regions, with the instance pill in the bottom-left showing the aggregated region + playground counts (in German, for example 2 Regionen · <count> Spielplätze, with a globe icon).
  3. Open DevTools → Network and reload. You should see:
  4. One GET /registry.json from the Hub's origin.
  5. One GET /rpc/get_meta per data-node, cross-origin, returning 200 with playground_count + bbox + completeness fields.
  6. On the first moveend, either GET /rpc/get_playground_clusters?... (cluster tier, zoom ≤ 13) or GET /rpc/get_playgrounds_bbox?... (polygon tier, zoom ≥ 14) per data-node whose bbox intersects the viewport. A data-node whose bbox sits entirely outside the viewport receives no request — that's the bbox router (see How the hub works internally) doing its job, not a bug.
  7. At zoom ≤ 7 (MACRO_MAX_ZOOM, the country view) you should see no per-playground requests at all while no filter is active — the country-level macro view renders entirely from the cached get_meta response. One ring per data-node. With a filter on, one get_playground_clusters request per data-node is expected: that is how the rings show filtered counts.
  8. Click the instance pill — the drawer lists both backends with their playground count, data age and release version (from each backend's get_meta).
  9. Click a playground in each region — the selection panel opens with that region's data.

If any data-node request fails in DevTools, the instance drawer marks that backend red with the error message. Check the data-node's CORS headers (Step 1 verification) and that its URL in registry.json is reachable from the browser, not only from the Hub host.

docs.title: Running Hub and data-nodes on the same host
docs.text:
Hub and data-nodes can share one machine, each as its own Compose project with its own APP_PORT and COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME. Two pages cover that case:

  • Single-host Federation: a hub plus many data-nodes on one VPS, including hardware sizing, port allocation and keeping imports apart.
  • Add a Data-node: adding one more region to a host that already runs a hub, including the reverse-proxy routes (subdomain or path prefix) and the matching registry.json entry.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• registry.json reference — full schema, slug rules, derived behaviours.
  • Federation: one map, many owners — why spieli is federated.
  • Federation reference — federation endpoints, zoom tiers, ring states.
  • Configuration — full variables table including REGISTRY_URL and HUB_POLL_INTERVAL.
  • Architecture — the DEPLOY_MODE × APP_MODE matrix that makes the legal combinations explicit.

docs.title: HTTPS setup (Traefik + Let's Encrypt)
docs.text: The spieli Docker stack listens on port 8080 over plain HTTP. To serve it publicly over HTTPS, use the deploy/traefik stack — a single Traefik v3 container that terminates TLS and reverse-proxies to port 8080. Traefik handles certificate issuance and renewal automatically — no certbot container, no manual cert steps.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A VM with a public IP address
  • Docker Engine 20.10+ and Docker Compose v2 (docker compose version)
  • A DNS A record pointing your domain to the server IP (e.g. spieli.example.com → 1.2.3.4)
  • Ports 80 and 443 open in the firewall (see Firewall)

docs.title: 1. Download and run the installer
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mfuhrmann/spieli/main/deploy/traefik/install-traefik.sh -o install-traefik.sh
bash install-traefik.sh

The installer prompts for an installation directory (default ./spieli-traefik), your domain, email address, and a mode, then:

  1. Downloads the Compose file
  2. Generates traefik.yml with your email for Let's Encrypt
  3. Generates dynamic/app.yml with your domain and routing rules
  4. Starts Traefik

Which mode to choose:

Your spieli DEPLOY_MODE Traefik mode data-node-ui 1 (data-node-ui, proxies to the app on port 8080) ui (a hub, or a remote frontend) 1 as well: the app is on port 8080 data-node 2 (data-node) — currently broken: it proxies to port 3000, which the installed stack does not publish (#1062). Run data-node-ui and mode 1 instead

Traefik issues the TLS certificate on the first HTTPS request (takes ~10 seconds). If your browser shows a certificate error immediately after startup, wait a moment and reload.

docs.title: 2. Install spieli
docs.text:
If you haven't installed the spieli app stack yet, follow Quick Start → Install. It installs a tagged release and verifies the installer's checksum.

When the spieli installer asks for the public URL of the instance (part of the imprint and privacy setup), enter https://spieli.example.com.

docs.title: Renewal
docs.text: Traefik renews certificates automatically before they expire. No cron jobs or manual steps needed.

docs.title: Stopping and starting
docs.text:
cd spieli-traefik
docker compose down   # stop
docker compose up -d  # start (cert is stored in the letsencrypt volume — no re-issue needed)

docs.title: Firewall
docs.text:
Open ports 80 (ACME challenge) and 443 (HTTPS). Block 8080 from public access — traffic should only reach it through Traefik. UFW alone does not do that: Docker opens published ports past UFW's rules, so block 8080 in your provider's firewall (or with a rule in iptables' DOCKER-USER chain).

ufw allow 80/tcp
ufw allow 443/tcp
ufw deny 8080/tcp

Cloud provider firewalls
