  python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('version:', d['version'], ' playgrounds:', d['playground_count'])"

Both version and playground_count should be non-zero. If playground_count is 0, see Troubleshooting → Map loads but shows no playgrounds.

Retry it for a few minutes if it fails: the daemon's startup apply from step 4 has to finish first, and until it does the API is legitimately unavailable.

Verifying after step 4 is deliberate. Verifying before it checks a stack whose last writer may still be the old image, and the old schema is internally consistent enough to pass.

To confirm the schema really is the new one, compare the version get_meta reports against the release you just installed:

curl -sf http://localhost:<port>/api/rpc/get_meta | \
  python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['version'])"

version comes from the image that last applied api.sql, so it is the one field that distinguishes "the new schema is in place" from "an older image applied last". Do not check for the presence of a column instead: a column added in an earlier release is present in both schemas, so the check passes on the old one and gives false assurance in exactly the failure mode #800 is about.

docs.title: requires-env-update
docs.text:
1. Read the release notes to find the new or removed variable.
  2. Update .env accordingly.
  3. Then proceed with the normal upgrade steps for your deployment type.

docs.title: requires-compose-update
docs.text:
compose.yml has structural changes (new service, renamed service, removed volume).

The installed compose.yml is the repository's compose.prod.yml, renamed. Fetch it from the release you are upgrading to, not from main, and not the repository's own compose.yml (that is the development stack):

TAG=vX.Y.Z   # the release you are upgrading to
cp compose.yml compose.yml.bak
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mfuhrmann/spieli/${TAG}/compose.prod.yml" -o compose.yml

# Recreate the stack:
docker compose --profile <mode> down
docker compose --profile <mode> up -d

Compare with compose.yml.bak for anything you changed by hand. On a hub set up by the installer that includes the registry.json bind-mount, which the installer enabled by uncommenting a line: uncomment it again.

Or re-run install.sh. It downloads the new compose.yml and keeps your database password and modes, but asks all other questions again and rewrites .env.

docs.title: requires-reimport
docs.text:
A new OSM tag type was added. Existing data doesn't have the new columns until a fresh import.

After the image update (Watchtower or manual steps 1–2), run one full import as described in Refresh Data — on a stack with automatic updates that means stopping the daemon first (Daemon mode). A full import also applies api.sql, so no separate API_ONLY=1 step is needed.

docs.title: Single-host federation (multiple stacks on one VPS)
docs.text: Several stacks on one host are upgraded with scripts/upgrade-stacks.sh, one stack at a time and in a fixed order. See Single-host Federation → Upgrading.

docs.title: Special cases
docs.text: If you deleted the database volume, see Refresh Data → After deleting the database.

docs.title: PostgreSQL major version
docs.text:
A release that moves to a new PostgreSQL major version (e.g. 16 → 17) carries requires-compose-update and requires-reimport, and its notes say so. The new PostgreSQL cannot read the old data directory, so the database volume is recreated and the data imported again — it all comes from OpenStreetMap, so nothing is lost:

docker compose --profile <mode> down
# fetch the new compose.yml as under requires-compose-update above
docker volume rm <project>_pgdata          # docker volume ls shows the exact name
docker compose --profile <mode> up -d

The import then starts as described in Refresh Data → After deleting the database. Back up first only if you keep data in the database that does not come from the import.

docs.title: Downgrading
docs.text:
Supported only within the same minor version. Pin a specific version by editing compose.yml:

# Change :latest to the version you want, for both images:
image: ghcr.io/mfuhrmann/spieli:0.4.0
image: ghcr.io/mfuhrmann/spieli-importer:0.4.0

docker compose pull
docker compose --profile <mode> up -d

The database schema is not automatically rolled back. If the new version added columns or functions, the older app typically ignores them — but this is not tested. When in doubt, re-import from scratch.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Configuration reference — check for new or changed variables before upgrading
  • Troubleshooting — common post-upgrade issues
  • Single-host Federation — multi-stack setup and the upgrade script
  • RELEASING.md — how releases are cut (maintainer reference)

docs.title: Watching your instance
docs.text: How to notice when your region stops answering or its data goes stale. This page is for the operator of a single instance (a data-node or a standalone map). Running a hub? Its endpoints and dashboard are described in Monitoring.

docs.title: If you host a region for spieli.eu
docs.text: Your region is already watched: the spieli.eu hub polls every region once a minute, and its dashboard at stats.spieli.eu shows whether yours is reachable, when it last imported and how many playgrounds it serves. Nobody alerts you from there, though. If you want to hear about an outage before your visitors do, add your own check as below.

docs.title: Your own check
docs.text:
Everything you need is in get_meta, which every instance answers:

curl -s https://<your-domain>/api/rpc/get_meta | python3 -m json.tool

Point any HTTP uptime tool (UptimeRobot, Better Stack, a cron job with curl) at that URL and check:

Field Healthy What a bad value means HTTP status 200 Not reachable, or PostgREST is down. A 404 before the first import has completed is expected. playground_count greater than 0 The import produced nothing: see Troubleshooting → Map loads but shows no playgrounds. data_age_seconds below your REIMPORT_INTERVAL_MAX_DAYS, plus REIMPORT_JITTER_HOURS and the import time The scheduled import has stopped running. Check docker compose logs importer. importing false most of the time true for hours on end: the import is stuck. See Troubleshooting → Hub drawer shows "updating" badge that never clears. version the release you installed An upgrade did not take effect: see Troubleshooting → A stack serves the old schema after an upgrade.

Every field is described in the API reference.

/metrics is for hubs

Every instance serves /metrics and /federation-status.json, but only a hub fills them. On a data-node or standalone map they hold a placeholder written once at startup, so a Prometheus scraping them sees no backends at all. Watch get_meta instead.

Frontend errors (JavaScript errors in visitors' browsers) are not reported anywhere by default; adding that needs your own image: see Customise your own image → Frontend error reporting.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: PostgREST exposes the functions of the api schema as endpoints under /api/rpc/ that return JSON. All endpoints accept GET requests with query-string parameters.

docs.title: Full RPC index
docs.text: RPC Used by Notes get_playground_clusters Standalone cluster tier zoom ≤ clusterMaxZoom get_playgrounds_bbox Standalone polygon tier zoom > clusterMaxZoom get_playground Deeplink restore single feature get_playground_centroids Lightweight per-playground rows not used by spieli's own frontend get_equipment PlaygroundPanel devices, pitches, benches within a bbox get_standalone_equipment Standalone pitch layer pitches/benches outside playgrounds get_pitch Pitch deeplink restore (#P<osm_id>) single standalone pitch get_pois PlaygroundPanel nearby toilets, bus stops, cafés get_trees PlaygroundPanel tree layer natural=tree nodes and natural=tree_row lines get_meta Hub federation discovery instance metadata + import freshness get_nearest_playgrounds Not used by the frontend since #949 ordered by distance get_playgrounds (deprecated) Legacy fallback region-scoped, deprecated

docs.title: Two-tier client contract
docs.text:
The standalone client renders playgrounds through two zoom-scoped layers:

Zoom Tier RPC ≤ clusterMaxZoom (default 13) cluster get_playground_clusters(z, bbox) > clusterMaxZoom polygon get_playgrounds_bbox(bbox)

Single-feature hydration on demand:

Use case RPC Deeplink restore at low zoom get_playground(osm_id)

A third bbox-scoped RPC, get_playground_centroids(bbox), returns one lightweight row per playground. Neither the standalone map nor the hub calls it (the hub merges cluster buckets instead, see How the hub works internally); it is there for other clients.

docs.title: get_playground_clusters(z, bbox)
docs.text:
Pre-aggregated cluster buckets for the cluster tier. Each bucket counts playgrounds whose centroid snaps to a zoom-appropriate grid cell, broken down by mapping detail.

Parameters

Name Type Default Notes z int — Zoom level — drives cell size via a hardcoded table (10 Mm at z=0, halving each level down to ~1.2 km at z=13) min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat float8 — WGS84 bounding box filter_private boolean false When true, exclude every playground that is not public: access = private, no or customers filter_hide_private boolean false When true, exclude only private playgrounds (access = private or no) and keep customers-only ones. Sent by the frontend's "No private ones" filter (#1002). A backend older than this parameter answers 404 PGRST202; the client then retries without it and stops sending it to that backend for the session. The filter is then not applied there at the cluster tier (bucket counts include private playgrounds, and buckets carry no access, so a bucket of one is an ordinary pin); only the polygon tier filters it client-side, and the hub's macro tier counts that backend as "can't filter" filter_water boolean false When true, include only water playgrounds filter_baby boolean false When true, include only baby-friendly playgrounds filter_toddler boolean false When true, include only toddler-friendly playgrounds filter_wheelchair boolean false When true, include only wheelchair-accessible playgrounds filter_bench boolean false When true, include only playgrounds with a bench filter_picnic boolean false When true, include only playgrounds with a picnic table filter_shelter boolean false When true, include only playgrounds with a shelter filter_table_tennis boolean false When true, include only playgrounds with a table tennis table filter_soccer boolean false When true, include only playgrounds with a football pitch filter_basketball boolean false When true, include only playgrounds with a basketball court filter_fence boolean false When true, include only playgrounds with a fence — own tags, or a separate barrier=fence way along ≥ 75 % of the outline (#773) filter_has_dogs boolean false When true, include only playgrounds where dogs are allowed filter_theme boolean false When true, include only playgrounds with a recognised playground:theme filter_shade boolean false When true, include only playgrounds with shade filter_lit boolean false When true, include only playgrounds whose has_lit is true filter_complete boolean true When false, exclude complete playgrounds filter_partial boolean true When false, exclude partial playgrounds filter_missing boolean true When false, exclude missing playgrounds

Response — JSON array of bucket objects:

[
  {
    "lon":         9.7140,
    "lat":         50.5489,
    "count":       2,
    "complete":    1,
    "partial":     0,
    "missing":     1
  }
]

Invariant: count = complete + partial + missing for every bucket. Every playground — including access-restricted ones — is counted into its completeness bucket; there is no separate restricted field. The filter_private parameter still excludes access-restricted playgrounds from the result when set.

Bucket centre: emitted lon / lat is the unweighted spatial mean of the bucket's member centroids (ST_Centroid(ST_Collect(centroid_3857)), reprojected to WGS84) — not the grid anchor. The grid still defines which playgrounds share a bucket (the grouping key), but the dot is drawn at the geographic mean of those members so it tracks settlements rather than a lattice. Output is deterministic for a given (z, bbox) and dataset: identical inputs produce identical positions. See Frontend Guide — Cluster buckets for the grouping-vs-position split.

Example

curl 'https://example.com/api/rpc/get_playground_clusters?z=12&min_lon=9&min_lat=50&max_lon=10&max_lat=51'

docs.title: get_playgrounds_bbox(bbox)
docs.text:
Polygon-tier RPC. Returns the same FeatureCollection shape as the legacy region-scoped get_playgrounds(relation_id), but restricted to playgrounds whose geometry intersects the bbox (so polygons straddling the viewport edge are returned in full).

Parameters

Name Type Notes min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat float8 WGS84 bounding box

Response — GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Each feature's properties include osm_id, osm_type (R, W, or N), name, leisure, operator, access, surface, area, the playground-stats counts (device_count, bench_count, shelter_count, picnic_count, table_tennis_count, and tree_count — natural=tree nodes within 15 m of the playground on the ground), and the per-equipment booleans (is_water, for_baby, for_toddler, for_wheelchair, has_soccer, has_basketball, has_fence, has_dogs, has_theme, has_shade, has_lit), plus the tri-state wheelchair_play ('yes' | 'no' | null). The original tag hstore is spread on top so any OSM tag is reachable. Node playgrounds (osm_type = 'N') are returned as small circular polygons (5 m radius buffer around the node point).

The equipment booleans are aggregated across all equipment within the playground polygon. for_baby is true when any equipment has baby=yes, capacity:baby set, or playground ∈ baby_swing, basketswing, sandpit, springy. See Import Pipeline — filter flags for the full trigger list.

for_wheelchair is the boolean projection of wheelchair_play, which is derived from play devices only — the playground area's own wheelchair tag is not an input, and street furniture and pitches cannot set it. wheelchair_play = 'no' means accessibility was surveyed and nothing qualified; null means nobody recorded it either way. The tri-state is carried by the per-feature RPCs only, not by the cluster, centroid or meta aggregates.

Note: the polygon RPC names the water flag is_water (legacy from the materialised-view column). The centroid RPC's filter_attrs payload (below) renames it to has_water for consistency with the other client-side filter keys (for_baby, has_soccer, …). Same boolean, different key.

{
  "type": "FeatureCollection",
  "features": [
    {
      "type": "Feature",
      "geometry": { "type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [...] },
      "properties": {
        "osm_id":             37808214,
        "osm_type":           "W",
        "name":               "Grezzbachpark",
        "leisure":            "playground",
        "operator":           "...",
        "access":             "yes",
        "surface":            "...",
        "area":               2480,
        "tree_count":         12,
        "bench_count":        4,
        "has_soccer":         true,
        "has_fence":          true,
        "has_dogs":           false,
        "has_theme":          false,
        "has_shade":          true,  // true | false | null (untagged)
        "has_lit":            null,  // true | false | null (untagged)
        "is_water":           true,
        "for_wheelchair":     false,
        "wheelchair_play":    null   // 'yes' | 'no' | null (never surveyed)
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: get_playground(osm_id)
docs.text:
Single-feature lookup used by the deeplink-hydration path when the polygon source isn't populated for the current viewport (cluster tier on first load).

Parameters

Name Type Notes osm_id bigint Magnitude only; the function tries both relation (-osm_id) and way (+osm_id) rows and prefers a relation row when both exist

Response — A single GeoJSON Feature with the same properties shape as one element of get_playgrounds_bbox.features[*], or JSON null when no playground matches.

Frontend convention: callers throw on non-2xx responses and treat a null body as a legitimate "not found", so server errors and missing playgrounds can be acted on differently.

docs.title: get_playground_centroids(bbox)
docs.text:
Returns lightweight per-playground rows for a bbox — osm_id, lon/lat, completeness, and a nested filter_attrs object (has_water, for_baby, for_toddler, for_wheelchair, has_soccer, has_basketball, access_restricted). No polygon geometry, no tag hstore.

[
  {
    "osm_id":       37808214,
    "lon":          9.7096,
    "lat":          50.5438,
    "completeness": "complete",
    "filter_attrs": {
      "has_water":         true,
      "for_baby":          false,
      "for_toddler":       false,
      "for_wheelchair":    false,
      "has_soccer":        true,
      "has_basketball":    false,
      "has_fence":         true,
      "has_dogs":          false,
      "has_theme":         false,
      "has_shade":         true,  // true | false | null (untagged)
      "has_lit":           null,  // true | false | null (untagged)
      "access_restricted": false
    }
  }
]

spieli's own frontend does not call it: the server-bucketed cluster tier covers zoom ≤ 13 in both modes, and the hub merges those buckets across backends. fetchPlaygroundCentroids() in app/src/lib/api.js exists but is unused.

Note: the filter_attrs object includes has_fence, has_dogs, has_theme, has_shade and has_lit for the playground filters. has_shade and has_lit are nullable — has_shade is true when shade=yes, false when shade=no; has_lit is true for a recognised lighting value (yes, 24/7, automatic, limited, interval, times), false for no / disused; each is null when untagged (has_lit also when the value is not recognised).

docs.title: Deprecated: get_playgrounds(relation_id)
docs.text:
The pre-tiered region-scoped RPC, deprecated since v0.3.0. It stays as the fallback a client or hub uses when a backend answers a tier RPC with 404, and for external consumers. Marked DEPRECATED via SQL COMMENT; the client fetchPlaygrounds logs a one-time console warning. No release for its removal is set.

Migration: replace any caller with fetchPlaygroundsBbox(extent, baseUrl) driven by viewport extent.

docs.title: get_equipment(bbox)
docs.text:
Returns all playground equipment within a WGS84 bounding box — devices (playground=*), pitches (leisure=pitch), benches (amenity=bench), shelters (amenity=shelter), fitness stations (leisure=fitness_station), and picnic tables (leisure=picnic_table).

Covers nodes, polygon ways, and linear ways. Used by PlaygroundPanel to populate the equipment list and overlay layers when a playground is selected.

Parameters

Name Type Notes min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat float8 WGS84 bbox — typically the selected playground's extent

Response — GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Each feature's properties include osm_id, osm_type (N or W), name, amenity, leisure, sport, surface, plus all OSM tags from the hstore column spread onto the properties object.

{
  "type": "FeatureCollection",
  "features": [
    {
      "type": "Feature",
      "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [9.71, 50.54] },
      "properties": {
        "osm_id":    12345678,
        "osm_type":  "N",
        "amenity":   null,
        "leisure":   null,
        "sport":     null,
        "playground": "slide",
        "height":    "1.2"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Example

curl 'https://example.com/api/rpc/get_equipment?min_lon=9.70&min_lat=50.53&max_lon=9.72&max_lat=50.55'

docs.title: get_standalone_equipment(bbox)
docs.text:
Returns pitches, benches, shelters, picnic tables, and fitness stations that do not lie within any leisure=playground polygon. Used by the standalone pitch layer (filterStore.standalonePitches).

Same parameter and response shape as get_equipment. Returns an empty FeatureCollection when apiBaseUrl is empty (Overpass fallback, used in local frontend dev without a database).

Each feature's properties carry osm_id, osm_type, name, amenity, leisure, sport, surface, access, operator, plus every other OSM tag of the object merged in (lit, panoramax, hoops, reservation, fee, opening_hours, wheelchair, …). access and operator were added for the pitch panel (#934) — they are osm2pgsql columns, so the merged tags never contained them.

Example

curl 'https://example.com/api/rpc/get_standalone_equipment?min_lon=9.60&min_lat=50.50&max_lon=9.80&max_lat=50.60'

docs.title: get_pitch(osm_id)
docs.text:
Single standalone pitch, used to restore a #P<osm_id> pitch link when the pitch layer has not loaded it yet (#934).

Parameters

Name Type Notes osm_id bigint Magnitude only; a polygon (way or relation) is preferred over a node with the same number

Response — A single GeoJSON Feature with the same properties shape as a pitch in get_standalone_equipment, or JSON null when there is no such pitch or it lies inside a playground (the same rule the pitch layer applies, so a link resolves exactly the pitches the layer shows).

Example

curl 'https://example.com/api/rpc/get_pitch?osm_id=923521639'

docs.title: get_pois(lat, lon, radius_m)
docs.text:
Returns nearby points of interest within radius_m metres of the given WGS84 point. Used by PlaygroundPanel to show nearby amenities.

Parameters

Name Type Default Notes lat float8 — WGS84 latitude lon float8 — WGS84 longitude radius_m integer 500 Search radius in ground metres, capped at 20 000 (the frontend sends POI_RADIUS_M, default 5000). Polygon POIs count when their centroid — the position returned — is in range. Before #954 it was compared in EPSG:3857 units, which made the effective radius radius_m × cos(latitude) — about 3.2 km for 5000 in central Germany

POI types returned:

Category OSM tag Toilets amenity=toilets Ice cream amenity=ice_cream or amenity=cafe/restaurant + cuisine=*ice_cream* Emergency emergency=yes + hospital/clinic, or healthcare:speciality=emergency Bus stop highway=bus_stop Pharmacy shop=chemist Supermarket / convenience / bakery shop=supermarket, shop=convenience, shop=bakery

Response — JSON array:

[
  {
    "osm_id":  987654321,
    "lat":     50.5421,
    "lon":     9.7133,
    "name":    "Spielplatz-WC",
    "amenity": "toilets",
    "shop":    null,
    "highway": null,
    "tags":    {}
  }
]

Example

curl 'https://example.com/api/rpc/get_pois?lat=50.54&lon=9.71&radius_m=300'

docs.title: get_trees(bbox)
docs.text:
Returns natural=tree nodes and natural=tree_row line features within a WGS84 bounding box. Used by PlaygroundPanel to populate the tree overlay layer when a playground is selected. Tree rows render as dark green lines on the map; the panel merges both signals into a single shade hint ("N trees / M m").

Parameters

Name Type Notes min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat float8 WGS84 bbox

Response — GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Point features (natural=tree) carry properties.osm_id, properties.name, plus OSM tags. LineString features (natural=tree_row) additionally carry properties.length_m (row length in metres, from ST_Length).

Example

curl 'https://example.com/api/rpc/get_trees?min_lon=9.70&min_lat=50.53&max_lon=9.72&max_lat=50.55'

docs.title: get_meta()
docs.text:
Returns instance metadata used by the Hub for federation discovery. Required for a backend to participate in a Hub.

Parameters: none (uses the configured OSM_RELATION_ID)

Response:

{
  "relation_id":          62700,
  "name":                 "Landkreis Fulda",
  "playground_count":     147,
  "complete":             42,
  "partial":              81,
  "missing":              24,
  "bbox":                 [9.43, 50.36, 10.08, 50.81],
  "last_import_at":       "2026-04-30T03:12:00Z",
  "data_age_seconds":     86400,
  "osm_data_timestamp":   "2026-04-29T21:00:00Z",
  "osm_data_age_seconds": 108000,
  "importing":            false,
  "version":              "0.4.1",
  "impressum_url":        "https://spieli.example.com/impressum",
  "privacy_url":          "https://spieli.example.com/datenschutz"
}

Field notes:

Field Notes playground_count Total playgrounds in the region. Equals complete + partial + missing. complete, partial, missing Completeness breakdown (access-restricted playgrounds roll into these counts, same as get_playground_clusters). bbox [west, south, east, north] in WGS84. null when the relation is not found. last_import_at When import.sh last ran successfully. null before any import. data_age_seconds Seconds since last_import_at. null when last_import_at is null. osm_data_timestamp PBF replication timestamp (when Geofabrik last generated the extract). null when the PBF header lacks this field. osm_data_age_seconds Seconds since osm_data_timestamp. null when osm_data_timestamp is null. importing true while osm2pgsql is actively running (data partially rebuilt); false at all other times. false on older backends that pre-date this field. The Hub drawer shows an "updating" badge while this is true. version spieli version string baked in at import time from package.json (e.g. "0.4.1"). Displayed in the Hub's instance drawer. impressum_url Absolute URL of the Impressum page. IMPRESSUM_URL env var takes priority; otherwise constructed from SITE_URL + /impressum. null when neither is configured. Baked in when api.sql is applied — re-apply it after changing legal env vars (see Configure the instance → Applying legal changes). privacy_url Absolute URL of the Datenschutzerklärung. PRIVACY_URL env var takes priority; otherwise SITE_URL + /datenschutz. null when neither is configured. has_legal true when the backend stores generated legal text in api.legal_content (written by a full import when IMPRESSUM_NAME and IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS are set). Lets the hub show the legal links via get_legal even when both URLs are null. region_geom GeoJSON geometry | null. Simplified boundary of the region (ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology at 0.05°, WGS84), used by the hub to detect a region lying entirely inside another (@turf/boolean-contains, checked both ways, in the browser). Regions that only partly overlap get no warning. null when the relation has no polygon; omitted by pre-0.4.13 backends, which then get no overlap warning.

The hub reads the import timestamps and importing through its own /federation-status.json (written every 60 seconds by the hub's cron poll, see Monitoring); counts, bbox and region_geom come from each browser's direct get_meta call.

Example

curl 'https://example.com/api/rpc/get_meta'

docs.title: get_legal(type)
docs.text:
Returns the legal HTML a data-node stored during its last full import. The Hub calls this when get_meta() returns a null impressum_url or privacy_url.

Parameters

Name Type Values type text 'impressum' or 'datenschutz'

Response — JSON object or null:

{ "content": "<html>...</html>" }

Returns null (HTTP 200) when no content has been stored for the requested type, that is, when no full import has run with IMPRESSUM_NAME and IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS set.

Example

curl 'https://example.com/api/rpc/get_legal?type=impressum'

docs.title: get_nearest_playgrounds(lat, lon)
docs.text:
Returns the nearest playgrounds to a WGS84 point, ordered by distance ascending. The frontend no longer calls it — the nearby list under the search field was removed (#949); it stays so hubs on older releases keep working.

Parameters

Name Type Default Notes lat float8 — WGS84 latitude lon float8 — WGS84 longitude relation_id bigint OSM_RELATION_ID Unused; kept for API compatibility. Like playground_stats, the search covers every playground the instance imported, not only those inside the boundary polygon max_results int 5 Maximum results, clamped to 1–50

Response — JSON array:

[
  {
    "osm_id":     37808214,
    "osm_type":   "W",
    "name":       "Grezzbachpark",
    "lat":        50.5438,
    "lon":        9.7096,
    "distance_m": 342,
    "completeness": "partial",
    "tags":       { "name": "Grezzbachpark", "operator": "…", "access": "yes" }
  }
]

completeness (complete | partial | missing) is the server-side mapping detail from playground_stats, the same value get_playground_centroids ships. Clients should prefer it over deriving one from tags: the tags carry no equipment counts, so a tag-derived value never sees mapped devices. Backends older than this field omit it.

osm_type (N | W | R) disambiguates osm_id, which is shown as an absolute value: node, way and relation ids are separate number spaces. Each playground appears once, also when it is a multipolygon relation with several outer rings. distance_m is measured to the playground's edge (0 when the point is inside it); playgrounds mapped as a node are measured to the node.

Example

curl 'https://example.com/api/rpc/get_nearest_playgrounds?lat=50.54&lon=9.71'

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: How the parts of a spieli instance fit together. The pages that follow build on this picture: Federation explains why regions live on separate servers, Privacy by design why the browser talks to only one of them.

docs.title: Standalone mode (default)
docs.text:
One region, one database. APP_MODE=standalone (the default).

flowchart TD
    browser["Browser<br/>(your phone or laptop)"]
    subgraph instance["spieli instance"]
        nginx["nginx<br/>serves the app, proxies /api/ and /ext/, caches"]
        postgrest["PostgREST<br/>turns SQL functions into HTTP endpoints"]
        db[("PostgreSQL/PostGIS<br/>the region's playground data")]
        importer["importer<br/>osmium + osm2pgsql"]
    end
    osm["OpenStreetMap extract<br/>(Geofabrik, re-imported every few days)"]
    services["background map · search · photos · reviews"]

    browser --> nginx
    nginx --> postgrest --> db
    osm --> importer --> db
    nginx -- "fetched server-side, cached,<br/>without the visitor's address" --> services

Your browser loads the app from nginx. When it needs playground data, it calls /api/, which nginx forwards to PostgREST. PostgREST runs a SQL function in PostgreSQL and returns the results as JSON — no custom server code needed. The data comes from the importer, which downloads the OpenStreetMap extract for the region, cuts the region out and loads it with osm2pgsql — on a schedule, or whenever you re-run it (Scheduled Import).

Everything else the map shows (the background map, search, photos, reviews) nginx fetches from the third-party services on the visitor's behalf and caches, so the browser contacts no one but this instance. Why: Privacy by design.

docs.title: Hub mode
docs.text:
Multiple regional instances aggregated onto one shared map. APP_MODE=hub.

flowchart TD
    browser["Browser"]
    hub["hub<br/>nginx: the app + registry.json<br/>(no database)"]
    subgraph a["data-node A"]
        a_nginx["nginx /api/"] --> a_pg["PostgREST"] --> a_db[("PostgreSQL<br/>region A")]
    end
    subgraph b["data-node B"]
        b_nginx["nginx /api/"] --> b_pg["PostgREST"] --> b_db[("PostgreSQL<br/>region B")]
    end

    browser -- "1. app + registry.json" --> hub
    browser -- "2. playground data" --> a_nginx
    browser -- "2. playground data" --> b_nginx

The browser merges the results from A and B.

The browser loads the app and registry.json from the hub, then fetches playground data directly from each data-node listed there, which is why every data-node's /api/ must be public and send CORS headers. The hub itself never relays playground data. Why it is built this way: Federation: one map, many owners. How the hub decides which data-nodes to ask: How the hub works internally. Setting one up: Federated Deployment.

docs.title: Deployment modes
docs.text:
Every role above is the same spieli release. Two settings decide which one a stack plays:

  • DEPLOY_MODE picks which containers run: data-node (database, importer, API), ui (the app only) or data-node-ui (all of them).
  • APP_MODE picks how the map behaves: standalone (one region) or hub (many regions from registry.json).

They are independent of each other: one decides where the code runs, the other what it does. The five combinations, and when to use which, are in Deployment modes.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Deployment modes — the five combinations and when to use which.
  • Federation reference — how the hub talks to data-nodes, zoom tiers and ring states.
  • For developers: Frontend Guide, Import Pipeline, API reference, and Local Development → Hub mode for the two-backend dev setup.

docs.title: Mapping detail
docs.text:
Every playground is assigned one of three mapping-detail states, based on how much of it has been mapped in OpenStreetMap. The state describes the map, not the playground — a playground in the lowest state is not a bad playground, it is one nobody has written up yet.

Mapping detail is off by default: the map is a plain finder for families, and visitors who map switch the colours on themselves (User Guide → Mapping detail colours).

docs.title: States
docs.text:
State (identifier) Label Rule complete detailed Both criteria satisfied partial basic Exactly one satisfied missing no details yet Neither satisfied

The names in the first column are what the data carries internally; visitors only ever see the labels. The criteria behind them follow below; how they are coloured, in Colours.

docs.title: Criteria
docs.text: A playground is judged on two things: whether its play equipment is mapped (any play device inside it, or a ball court), and whether it has any detail — its surface, opening hours, or restricted access. One qualifying item is enough on each side; a playground needs only one of the three details, not all of them. The exact tags: OSM Tags spieli Reads → Mapping detail.

docs.title: What does not count as equipment
docs.text:
Street furniture — amenity=bench, amenity=shelter, leisure=picnic_table — is excluded. These are frequently mapped inside a playground area by someone who never mapped the play equipment itself, so counting them lifted playgrounds that have nothing to play on. In Fulda, 63 of 221 playgrounds registering as "has equipment" were carried by furniture alone.

Pitches do count: a football pitch or a basketball hoop is real play infrastructure, merely tagged leisure=pitch rather than playground=*.

Derived flags — is_water, for_baby, for_toddler, for_wheelchair — are also excluded. A genuine playground device already satisfies the playground=* test, so they add nothing there; on their own they can be set by a bench tagged wheelchair=yes, which is the same false signal (#776). They remain available as filter flags, they just do not feed the state.

docs.title: Photos are not a criterion
docs.text:
A photo (panoramax / panoramax:*, wikimedia_commons, or an image link on a Wikimedia/Wikipedia host) is not an input to the state.

It used to be: the old rule required all three of photo, equipment and info for the top state. Photo tags are rare in OSM, so that gated entire regions out of it — Hessen sat at 87 of 8802 playgrounds (1.0%) in the top bucket, while a well-photographed region reached 8.0% under the identical rule. A playground with twelve mapped devices plus surface and access stayed in the middle state indefinitely because nobody had uploaded a picture, which judged the mapper rather than the map (#733).

Photo availability is still surfaced, as an additive marker: a camera glyph drawn on the playground. Having a photo is a bonus; not having one is not a penalty.

The marker lives on the map only. There is no photo badge in the detail panel — by the time the panel is open the photos themselves are visible in it, so a chip announcing them would be redundant. On the map it is the only way to see which playgrounds have pictures without opening each one.

An off-Wikimedia image URL does not count — the gallery cannot render it.

docs.title: Hints in the panel
docs.text:
With mapping detail on, the playground panel shows a highlighted hint under the badge naming what is missing (#919). It is derived from the same rule as the badge, so the two cannot disagree:

Badge Missing Hint no details yet both Not mapped yet: play equipment, and the surface or opening hours (if it has any). basic equipment Not mapped yet: the play equipment. basic info Not mapped yet: the surface or opening hours (if it has any). detailed – (none)

The hint carries no link of its own: the panel's MapComplete links further down already open this playground. The list is closed on purpose: only surface and opening hours are named, because a vaguer "general details" would send mappers to name or operator, which do not count. Surface comes first because it can be checked on site and is unambiguous; opening hours carry "if it has any", since many playgrounds legitimately have none and the hint must not invite invented ones. Restricted access also counts but is not named — it describes the place, it is not something to add. By the rule's design, once one device is mapped there is no equipment hint even if more are missing, and "detailed" does not mean complete.

docs.title: Colours
docs.text:
The palette is a single-hue green ramp ending in a cool slate, not a traffic light. A diverging red/amber/green scale encodes "good versus bad", which reads as a verdict on the playground. This one encodes "more versus less", which is what the value measures.

Ordering is by lightness, and monotonic: complete L* 79, partial L* 47, missing L* 36. The brightest step marks the best-mapped playgrounds, and a viewer with deuteranopia or protanopia can recover the ordering without relying on the green-versus-slate hue split.

The zero case is a cool slate rather than a plain grey: neutral enough to read as "nothing here yet" instead of "bad", but with enough blue cast to stand out from the basemap's own warm greys (residential #e0dfdf, buildings #d9d0c9), which a plain grey at low alpha disappeared into.

On the map, the coloured ring segments carry a thin dark outline. Bright green alone is too faint against the background map, so the outline carries the contrast and the colours can be chosen for their meaning. The measurements behind this are in Frontend Guide → The mapping-detail palette.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text: How the rule is implemented and kept in sync between frontend and database: Import Pipeline → Mapping detail rule. Store, palette and locale keys: Frontend Guide → The finder view.

docs.title: Deployment modes
docs.text:
Every spieli stack runs the same release. Two settings decide which role it plays; the installer asks for both, and they end up in .env.

DEPLOY_MODE decides which containers run; APP_MODE decides how the map behaves. They are independent, which gives five combinations:

Scenario DEPLOY_MODE APP_MODE What starts Use when Standalone (default) data-node-ui standalone database, importer, API, app One self-contained map for your region. A hub can list it as well; nothing extra to set Backend only data-node — database, importer, API Provide a region to a hub without a map of your own. Needs a reverse proxy that adds CORS to the API. The Traefik installer's data-node mode currently cannot reach the API (#1062); until that is fixed, use Standalone with Traefik instead Remote frontend ui standalone app A map for one region whose data lives on another server. The installer asks for its API_BASE_URL; that server must send CORS headers Hub only ui hub app One map over several regions, each on its own data-node. No database of its own Hub + local backend data-node-ui hub database, importer, API, app A hub that also serves one region itself; registry.json lists the local /api plus any remote ones

For the hub scenarios the installer asks for REGISTRY_URL and writes a starter registry.json; edit it afterwards to list your data-nodes. How a hub works: Federation: one map, many owners.

APP_MODE is not asked for data-node, which has no frontend.

docs.title: Compose profiles
docs.text:
Each DEPLOY_MODE is a compose profile of the same name, so every docker compose command takes --profile <mode>:

Profile Starts data-node db, importer, postgrest — no frontend data-node-ui db, importer, postgrest, app ui app only, talking to the API in API_BASE_URL auto-update Watchtower, which installs new spieli images from GHCR once a day. Added on top of the mode (--profile data-node-ui --profile auto-update); the installer enables it when you choose automatic updates, and then also sets REIMPORT_INTERVAL_* so the importer runs in daemon mode. Only one per host: Upgrading → Automatic upgrade

docs.title: Supported Equipment Types
docs.text:
This page documents every equipment type that spieli recognises. The definitions live in two source files:

  • app/src/lib/objPlaygroundEquipment.js — objDevices, objFitnessStation, objFeatures
  • app/src/lib/equipmentAttributes.js — pitchImages

These tables decide a feature's symbol, label and example image. An OSM value not listed here still shows, with less information: see Fallback behaviour. Which tags make a playground match a filter or count for mapping detail: OSM Tags spieli Reads.

docs.text:
Keyed by the OSM playground=* tag value. 85 entries, grouped by category, which decides the device's symbol in the equipment list and on the map. Labels come from equipment.devices.<key> in the locale files (English and German shown here); the name_de field in objDevices is only the last fallback. "Image" marks entries with an example illustration.

Some keys cover mappers who use a generic value instead of a specific one (balance, climbing, rotator, water, sand); they are listed under their category.

docs.text:
An OSM tag not present in these objects still renders on the map and in the equipment list, but with reduced information:

  • Map icon: the generic fallback symbol
  • Label: the tag value tidied up (underscores to spaces, first letter capitalised), unless a locale file has a translation for it

docs.title: External Services
docs.text:
Every third-party service spieli uses, who contacts it, and how to change that. Why it is built this way: Privacy by design. The settings: Basemap and external services.

In a default deployment the visitor's browser contacts only this instance; the instance fetches the rest server-side, through a cache, without the visitor's address. Only two services are reached by the browser directly, and only in specific situations.

docs.title: Contacted by the browser directly
docs.text:
Service Host When Why it is not proxied Switch off Panoramax api.panoramax.xyz, which redirects thumbnails to a per-instance host (e.g. panoramax.openstreetmap.fr) Thumbnails: when a playground with street-level photos is opened. The viewer iframe: only after the visitor clicks the thumbnail, until they close it The redirect targets are a federation's hosts, not ours to enumerate, and nginx cannot follow a redirect; the viewer is a whole application that must not run on this origin (#863). The viewer sets an analytics cookie of its own, which is why it waits for a click: Privacy by design → What still leaves — OpenStreetMap notes api.openstreetmap.org (OSM_NOTES_URL) A "Missing a playground?" hint, only on Send; a sent hint's status, only when its pin is tapped Through one server, every anonymous note would come from one address, which OSM's spam limits block (#1000) OSM_NOTES_URL=false

Both are named in the generated Content Security Policy and on the generated privacy page.

docs.title: Fetched server-side (proxied)
docs.text:
Served to the browser from same-origin paths, cached on this instance. Opting a service out makes the browser contact its host directly; the generated CSP and privacy page then name it (Security → nginx security headers).

Service Host Used for Same-origin path Opt out with Background map (OpenFreeMap / OpenMapTiles by default) BASEMAP_UPSTREAM, default tiles.openfreemap.org Tiles, sprites, style /basemap/ BASEMAP_URL / BASEMAP_STYLE_URL pointing at a third party (needs BASEMAP_ATTRIBUTION) Nominatim nominatim.openstreetmap.org Place search; region names for URLs like /fulda /ext/nominatim/ PROXY_NOMINATIM=false Wikimedia Commons commons.wikimedia.org (API), upload.wikimedia.org, thumb.wikimedia.org (files) Playground photo gallery; device and pitch illustrations /ext/commons/, /ext/wikimedia/<host>/ PROXY_COMMONS=false OpenStreetMap wiki wiki.openstreetmap.org 14 device illustrations that exist only there /ext/wikimedia/<host>/ PROXY_COMMONS=false Mangrove.reviews api.mangrove.reviews Reading and submitting reviews. Proxied (default): read on selecting a playground, for the rating under its name. With the proxy off: only once the reviews section is opened /ext/mangrove/ PROXY_MANGROVE=false

What every proxy guarantees: no access log, no cookie, referrer, browser language or forwarded address on the outbound request, and no fallback to a direct connection when the upstream fails. Nominatim requests are limited to one per second, as its usage policy requires; cached answers are not counted. Details: Privacy by design and Basemap and external services → External-service proxies.

Serving the illustrations through this instance makes the operator their distributor, so the CC attribution is shown under each one where the wiki provides it; the OSM wiki provides none for its 14 files.

docs.title: Contacted only by the server
docs.text: Service Purpose Geofabrik OSM extracts (PBF_URL), downloaded by the importer Nominatim The importer looks up the region's bounding box once per import, unless OSM_BBOX is set

docs.title: Linked, not embedded
docs.text:
Reached only when the visitor clicks a link; nothing is transferred before that.

Service Purpose MapComplete Contribute photos and equipment Wikidata Operator entity linking OpenStreetMap Source data, editing, directions

docs.title: Stored in the browser
docs.text: A key pair for signing reviews is created in localStorage on the visitor's first review, not before. Everything spieli keeps in the browser: Privacy by design → What stays in your browser.

docs.title: Federation
docs.text: A hub is the same spieli release with APP_MODE=hub (Deployment modes). It reads its data-nodes from a registry.json and fetches their data from the visitor's browser. This page is the technical reference: what the hub asks each data-node, and what its rings mean. For why spieli is federated, see Federation: one map, many owners. To set a hub up, see Federated Deployment; to run one locally for development, see Local Development → Hub mode.

docs.title: Federation endpoints
docs.text:
A data-node joins a hub by answering these RPCs under its public /api/, with CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) so the hub's visitors can call them from the browser. Full request and response shapes: API reference.

Endpoint The hub uses it for get_meta Registry discovery and the macro tier: name, playground count, bounding box, mapping-detail counts, data age, version, legal links get_playground_clusters Cluster tier (zoom ≤ clusterMaxZoom), with the active filters as parameters get_playgrounds_bbox Polygon tier (zoom > clusterMaxZoom) get_playground Restoring a playground deep link at any zoom get_equipment, get_trees, get_pois The panel of a selected playground get_standalone_equipment The Sports pitches (outside playgrounds) layer get_pitch Restoring a pitch deep link (#<slug>/P<id>); a backend without it answers 404 and is skipped get_legal The region's legal text, when it has has_legal but no legal URLs get_playgrounds Deprecated fallback: used once per backend and session if a tier RPC answers 404, with a one-time warning

Backends older than the tiered API (before v0.4.9) still join: the cluster tier skips them rather than fetching the whole region through the legacy RPC only to discard it, and the macro view marks them (see Ring states).

docs.title: Hub UI
docs.text:
The hub looks like a regional map, plus a region pill and list at the bottom left and one ring per region when zoomed out. What visitors see and what the ring labels mean: User Guide → The all-regions map. The ring states and the conditions behind them are listed under Ring states below; deep-link forms in the registry.json reference.

Two signals in the region list are meant for hub operators: a region whose boundary lies entirely inside another's, or contains it (from region_geom in get_meta), carries an "overlaps with …" badge — a partial overlap is not detected — and if registry.json itself cannot be loaded the pill reads "Registry unreachable".

docs.title: Ring states
docs.text:
At zoom ≤ macroMaxZoom the Hub renders one ring per registered backend, sized by playground_count and segmented by the {complete, partial, missing} counts from get_meta. Without an active filter no per-playground fetch is issued at this zoom — the rings come entirely from the cached registry metadata. With a filter active, the hub asks each in-scope backend for get_playground_clusters at macroMaxZoom and sums the buckets, so the ring counts reflect the filter.

Clicking a ring animates view.fit to the backend's bbox, which lands in the cluster or polygon tier and triggers a tier fetch scoped to that backend only.

With mapping detail off (the default, #924) a healthy backend is a plain emerald disc with its count; the segmented ring below appears only while mapping detail is on. "Unfiltered" likewise draws the disc instead of the segments; the other states look the same in both views.

Each ring has one of these visual states, driven by federation-status.json (see Hub Status and Metrics), the cached get_meta response and, with a filter active, the filtered fan-out:

State Visual Condition Healthy Mapping-detail segments (light green / dark green / slate, see Colours; flat violet when the backend predates the completeness counts) + count in centre; an emerald disc with mapping detail off Backend reachable, data present Offline Dashed gray ring + last-known count + "offline" label federation-status.json reports up: false Importing Solid blue ring + count + "updating" label Backend reachable, osm2pgsql actively running Degraded Solid amber ring + "no data" label Backend reachable, not importing, but playground count is zero Unfiltered Full ring + dashed grey halo + "unfiltered" label A filter is active but this backend could not apply it (no bbox, or an older release), so its whole catalogue is shown No match Grey ring + "no match" label Healthy backend, but the active filter excludes every playground

Backends older than v0.4.9, whose get_meta lacks the mapping-detail counts, render as a flat violet ring (the whole count in the "unknown" slot, internally restricted) so the operator sees "mapping detail unknown" rather than a misleading all-zero healthy ring.

How the hub decides which backends to ask at which zoom, and how it merges their answers: How the hub works internally.

  • Federated Deployment — step-by-step walkthrough for standing up one Hub + N data-nodes.
  • registry.json reference — registry schema, slug rules, derived aggregate behaviours.
  • Monitoring — /federation-status.json and /metrics exposition, uptime and Prometheus recipes.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Terms you meet in spieli's map, docs and configuration, each with a pointer to where it is explained.

docs.title: Data-node
docs.text: A spieli stack with a database: it imports one region from OpenStreetMap and serves it through its API (DEPLOY_MODE=data-node or data-node-ui). With data-node-ui it also serves a map of its own. See Federation: one map, many owners.

docs.title: Hub
docs.text: A spieli stack in APP_MODE=hub that shows many regions on one map. It holds no playground data; visitors' browsers fetch it from the data-nodes listed in its registry. spieli.eu is a hub. See Federation: one map, many owners.

docs.title: Standalone
docs.text: APP_MODE=standalone, the default: a map of the single region the stack's own (or one remote) API serves. See Deployment modes.

docs.title: Registry
docs.text: The registry.json a hub reads to know its data-nodes: one entry with URL, name and slug per region. See registry.json reference.

docs.title: Slug
docs.text: The short, stable name of a region in a hub's registry (hessen), used in shared links such as #hessen/W37808214. See registry.json → Slug validation.

docs.title: Mapping detail
docs.text: How much of a playground has been mapped in OpenStreetMap: detailed, basic or no details yet (internally complete, partial, missing). Shown only when switched on; it rates the map, not the playground. See Mapping detail and, for the exact tags, OSM Tags spieli Reads.

docs.title: Finder view
docs.text: The default look of the map, with mapping detail off: neutral green circles and pins. See User Guide → Navigating the map.

docs.title: DEPLOY_MODE and APP_MODE
docs.text: The two settings that decide a stack's role. DEPLOY_MODE picks which containers run (data-node, ui, data-node-ui), APP_MODE how the map behaves (standalone, hub). See Deployment modes.

docs.title: Tiers: macro, cluster, polygon
docs.text: How the map loads playgrounds depending on the zoom level. Zoomed out (up to zoom 13 by default) it shows clusters, counts the server has already grouped; zoomed in, the polygon tier shows each playground. A hub adds the macro tier below that (up to zoom 7): one ring per region, drawn from numbers it already has. See Federation reference → Ring states.

docs.title: Ring
docs.text: The circle a hub draws for a region at the macro tier, sized by its playground count. Its look says whether the region is healthy, offline, updating or empty. See Federation reference → Ring states.

docs.title: External-service proxy
docs.text: The paths under /ext/ through which an instance fetches search, photos and reviews on the visitor's behalf, so the browser does not contact those services itself. The basemap works the same way under /basemap/. See External Services.

docs.title: Daemon mode
docs.text: The importer container running permanently and re-importing every few days on its own, instead of once (one-shot). Switched on by REIMPORT_INTERVAL_MIN_DAYS / MAX_DAYS; the installer does this when you choose automatic updates. See Scheduled Import.

docs.title: Watchtower
docs.text: The container (compose profile auto-update) that installs new spieli releases automatically. See Upgrading → Automatic upgrade.

docs.title: OSM relation ID
docs.text: Every city, district or region in OpenStreetMap has a numeric relation ID. A data-node uses it to cut its region out of the extract and to name it. Find it on Nominatim or openstreetmap.org: openstreetmap.org/relation/62700 → 62700. See Quick Start → Finding your region.

docs.title: PBF file
docs.text: A compressed snapshot of OpenStreetMap data for a region (Protocol Buffer Binary Format). Geofabrik publishes daily extracts at download.geofabrik.de. The importer reads one; it only needs to contain your region.

docs.title: osm2pgsql
docs.text: The tool that loads a PBF file into PostgreSQL. It runs inside the importer container, on every import. More: osm2pgsql.org.

docs.title: PostgREST
docs.text: A server that turns SQL functions into an HTTP API. spieli's whole API is PostgREST over the functions in importer/api.sql; there is no other backend application. More: postgrest.org.

docs.title: Overpass Turbo
docs.text: A web tool for ad-hoc queries against live OpenStreetMap data, at overpass-turbo.eu. Useful to find playgrounds with a particular tag, for testing or before adding a device type.

docs.title: Hub status and metrics
docs.text:
A hub container publishes two endpoints about the regions it lists. Both are written atomically every 60 seconds by a cron job inside the container, need no authentication, and are served with Cache-Control: no-store.

Endpoint Format Purpose /federation-status.json JSON Human-readable per-backend rollup; also read by the hub's own UI /metrics Prometheus text Scrape target for Prometheus/Grafana stacks

How to watch them — uptime checks, Prometheus alerts, the bundled Grafana dashboard: Monitoring.

docs.title: /federation-status.json
docs.text:
{
  "generated_at": "2026-04-26T12:00:00Z",
  "poll_interval_seconds": 60,
  "backends": {
    "fulda": {
      "url": "https://fulda.example.com/api",
      "up": true,
      "latency_seconds": 0.043,
      "last_success": "2026-04-26T12:00:00Z",
      "last_import_at": "2026-04-25T03:12:00Z",
      "data_age_seconds": 118080,
      "osm_data_timestamp": "2026-04-24T21:00:00Z",
      "osm_data_age_seconds": 140400,
      "playground_count": 42,
      "complete": 28,
      "partial": 10,
      "missing": 4
    }
  }
}

Fields:

Field Notes generated_at ISO 8601 timestamp when this file was written. Use this to detect a frozen hub (generated_at older than 2 × poll_interval_seconds). poll_interval_seconds Always 60 in the current release. backends.<slug>.up true if the backend responded to GET /rpc/get_meta within 3 s. backends.<slug>.latency_seconds Round-trip time of the last successful poll. 0 on failure. backends.<slug>.last_success ISO 8601 timestamp of the last successful probe, preserved across failures. null if the backend was never reachable. backends.<slug>.last_import_at Value of api.import_status.last_import_at from the backend DB. null if no import has run or backend is down. backends.<slug>.data_age_seconds Seconds since last_import_at. null if last_import_at is null. backends.<slug>.osm_data_timestamp Replication timestamp of the OSM extract the backend imported (when Geofabrik generated it). null if the PBF header lacks it, the backend predates the field, or it is down. backends.<slug>.osm_data_age_seconds Seconds since osm_data_timestamp — how old the served data is, which is always at least data_age_seconds. null when osm_data_timestamp is. backends.<slug>.playground_count Total playgrounds in the region. null on backends older than v0.4.9 or when backend is down. backends.<slug>.complete Playgrounds with detailed mapping: play equipment and info (opening_hours, surface or access). null on backends older than v0.4.9. backends.<slug>.partial Playgrounds with basic mapping: play equipment or info, not both. null on backends older than v0.4.9. backends.<slug>.missing Playgrounds with no details yet: neither play equipment nor info. null on backends older than v0.4.9. backends.<slug>.importing true while the backend's importer is running osm2pgsql. false on backends that predate the field. backends.<slug>.version The spieli release the backend runs, from its get_meta. null when down or unknown. backends.<slug>.impressum_url / privacy_url The backend's legal pages, from its get_meta. null when not configured. backends.<slug>.has_legal true when the backend stores generated legal text (api.legal_content); the hub then shows the legal links even without URLs.

The cron job rewrites this file every 60 seconds; browsers re-read it every HUB_POLL_INTERVAL seconds (default 300) and show its freshness labels in the region list. When generated_at is older than 2 × poll_interval_seconds (the hub cron has stopped writing), the list marks the data "Observation status outdated".

docs.title: /metrics
docs.text:
Prometheus text exposition format (version 0.0.4):

# HELP spielplatz_backend_up 1 if the backend responded to get_meta, 0 otherwise.
# TYPE spielplatz_backend_up gauge
spielplatz_backend_up{backend="fulda",url="https://fulda.example.com/api"} 1

# HELP spielplatz_backend_importing 1 while osm2pgsql is actively running on this backend, 0 otherwise.
# TYPE spielplatz_backend_importing gauge
spielplatz_backend_importing{backend="fulda",url="https://fulda.example.com/api"} 0

# HELP spielplatz_backend_latency_seconds Round-trip time for the last get_meta call.
# TYPE spielplatz_backend_latency_seconds gauge
spielplatz_backend_latency_seconds{backend="fulda",url="https://fulda.example.com/api"} 0.043

# HELP spielplatz_backend_data_age_seconds Seconds since the backend last imported data.
# TYPE spielplatz_backend_data_age_seconds gauge
spielplatz_backend_data_age_seconds{backend="fulda",url="https://fulda.example.com/api"} 118080

# HELP spielplatz_backend_osm_data_age_seconds Seconds since the OSM source data the backend serves was snapshotted (PBF replication timestamp).
# TYPE spielplatz_backend_osm_data_age_seconds gauge
spielplatz_backend_osm_data_age_seconds{backend="fulda",url="https://fulda.example.com/api"} 140400

# HELP spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_total Total number of playgrounds in the region.
# TYPE spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_total gauge
spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_total{backend="fulda",url="https://fulda.example.com/api"} 42

# HELP spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_complete Playgrounds with detailed mapping: play equipment and info (opening_hours, surface or access).
# TYPE spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_complete gauge
spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_complete{backend="fulda",url="https://fulda.example.com/api"} 28

# HELP spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_partial Playgrounds with basic mapping: play equipment or info, not both.
# TYPE spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_partial gauge
spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_partial{backend="fulda",url="https://fulda.example.com/api"} 10

# HELP spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_missing Playgrounds with no details yet: neither play equipment nor info.
# TYPE spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_missing gauge
spielplatz_backend_playgrounds_missing{backend="fulda",url="https://fulda.example.com/api"} 4

# HELP spielplatz_poll_generated_timestamp Unix timestamp when this scrape was generated.
# TYPE spielplatz_poll_generated_timestamp gauge
spielplatz_poll_generated_timestamp 1745668800

spielplatz_backend_data_age_seconds, spielplatz_backend_osm_data_age_seconds and the four completeness gauges are omitted for a backend when the field is null (backend down, backend older than v0.4.9, or no import yet). spielplatz_backend_importing is always emitted when the backend is reachable; it defaults to 0 for older backends that predate the importing field in get_meta.

docs.title: OSM Tags spieli Reads
docs.text:
Which OpenStreetMap tags change what spieli shows, and how. This is the contract between mappers and the map: if a playground looks wrong in spieli, the tags below are what to check. All rules are implemented in importer/api.sql (the playground_stats view), some mirrored in the frontend; a change to a rule changes this page.

Why the rules are what they are is explained elsewhere: Mapping detail, User Guide → Wheelchair accessibility.

docs.title: Playgrounds and what belongs to them
docs.text:
What Tag Notes A playground leisure=playground, as an area or a node A node is treated as a circle of 5 m radius, so only equipment within 5 m of it counts — map the area where you can Its equipment any object whose geometry intersects the playground area Points inside, or ways and areas overlapping it Trees natural=tree nodes and natural=tree_row ways around the playground Drawn when the playground is open; its tree count uses natural=tree within 15 m of the area A fence around it see Fenced below A pitch outside any playground leisure=pitch not intersecting a playground area Shown on the Sports pitches (outside playgrounds) layer

What each device, fitness station and pitch is called and how it is grouped: Equipment Types.

docs.title: Mapping detail
docs.text:
Two criteria, each met by any one qualifying tag:

Criterion Met when Play equipment Inside the area there is an object tagged playground=*, or a leisure=pitch with sport=soccer, basketball/streetball or table_tennis Info The playground area carries opening_hours, surface, or access with a value other than yes

Both → detailed, one → basic, neither → no details yet. Not counted: benches, shelters and picnic tables (amenity=bench, amenity=shelter, leisure=picnic_table), and photos.

docs.title: Who may use it
docs.text:
From access on the playground area:

access spieli shows Hidden by Public only Hidden by No private ones unset, yes, anything else public no no customers for customers & guests only (cup badge) yes no private, no private (grey pin, lock) yes yes

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Filter Matches when Water playground A device inside has a playground value containing water, or playground=splash_pad / pump Baby-friendly A device inside has baby=yes, or is playground=baby_swing, basketswing, sandpit or springy, or carries capacity:baby Toddler-friendly A device inside has provided_for:toddler=yes, or is playground=basketswing Wheelchair-friendly A play device (playground=*) inside carries wheelchair=yes, limited or designated; a playground=sandpit counts only with wheelchair=yes. The area's own wheelchair tag, benches and pitches do not count. If devices carry wheelchair tags but none qualifies, the panel says No wheelchair equipment; if none carries one, it says nothing. A sandpit tagged anything other than wheelchair=yes does not count as surveyed, so a playground whose only tagged device is such a sandpit shows nothing either With bench amenity=bench inside With picnic table leisure=picnic_table inside With shelter amenity=shelter inside Table tennis table leisure=pitch + sport=table_tennis inside With football pitch leisure=pitch + sport=soccer inside Basketball court leisure=pitch + sport=basketball or streetball inside Fenced The area has enclosed=yes or barrier=fence, or separately mapped barrier=fence ways run within 4 m of at least 75 % of its outline Dogs allowed dog=yes on the area Themed An allowlisted playground:theme on the area or on a device inside (see below) With shade shade=yes on the area. The panel reads the tag itself: yes Shaded, partial Partly shaded, no No shade, untagged nothing (the filter does not match partial yet, #1072) Lit at night lit on the area reads as lit (see below)

Values separated by ; are split for sport and playground:theme.

docs.title: Activities and highlights (detail panel)
docs.text:
The panel's What kids can do row and its highlights line are derived from the play devices inside the playground — separately mapped playground=* objects and playground:<device>=yes|<n> on the area itself. Each device type in app/src/lib/objPlaygroundEquipment.js declares its activity and whether it is a highlight:

Activity Devices (playground=*) Swing swing, baby_swing, basketswing, tire_swing, rope_swing Slide slide Rock seesaw, springy Climb climbingframe, climbingwall, climbing_slope, climbing_pole, monkey_bars, climbing, mound, dome Balance balancebeam, rope_traverse, stepping_stone, stepping_post, balance, agility_trail, wobble_bridge, belt_bridge Spin roundabout, basketrotator, aerialrotator, spinner, spinning_disc, spinning_circle, spinner_bowl, rotator Bounce trampoline, cushion, spring_board, hopscotch Exercise horizontal_bar, parallel_bars, bannister_bars, hamster_wheel, exercise Dig sandpit, chute, sieve, sand_wheel, sand_seesaw, sand_pulley, excavator, table, sand Explore playhouse, tunnel_tube

Structure parts (structure, platform, ladder, steps, bridge) and water devices are no activity.

Highlights, in this order: the playground's theme; Water play once for any water device (category water, or the server's water flag); then, in catalogue order, aerialrotator, hamster_wheel, zipwire, trampoline, speaking_tube, funnel_ball, ball_pool, marble_run, musical_instrument, sledding.

docs.title: Lighting (lit)
docs.text:
Read case-insensitively, on playgrounds and on standalone pitches alike:

Value Read as yes, 24/7, automatic, limited, interval lit any value containing a digit, sunset or sunrise (e.g. sunset-22:00) lit no, disused not lit unset, or anything else unknown — shown as nothing

docs.title: Themes (playground:theme)
docs.text: Only these values count: ship, castle, spiderweb, water, adventure, rocket, dragon, octopus, circus. Others — including the shape of a single spring rider (horse, duck, …) — are ignored. On the area they produce a banner in the panel; on a device, a symbol next to it.

docs.title: Photos
docs.text:
The camera marker on the map, and the panel's photo section, come from tags on the playground:

Tag Shown as panoramax, panoramax:* street-level photos (Panoramax) wikimedia_commons Commons gallery (a file or a category) image pointing at a Wikimedia/Wikipedia file (an upload. URL or an image file extension) Commons gallery

An image link to anywhere else, or to a wiki page, is ignored. Photos are not part of mapping detail.

docs.title: Region boundary
docs.text: The region of a data-node is the OSM relation in OSM_RELATION_ID (usually a boundary=administrative relation). It is used to cut the region out of the extract and for the region's name and outline in get_meta; playgrounds are not filtered against the boundary afterwards.

docs.title: Paths and ports
docs.text: What a spieli instance serves, and under which path. Useful when you put your own reverse proxy, firewall or monitoring in front of it.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Port What Exposed by default APP_PORT (default 8080) on the host → 80 in the app container Everything below: the map, the API, the proxies Yes — the only published port 5432 (PostgreSQL), 3000 (PostgREST) Database and API server, inside the Docker network No; nginx reaches PostgREST internally

With the bundled Traefik (HTTPS setup), ports 80 and 443 are Traefik's and forward to APP_PORT.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
Path What Present on Browser caching / The map (static build) every instance with the app container index.html: no cache header; scripts, styles, images and fonts: one year /api/ PostgREST, the API. Sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * so a hub can read it data-nodes (data-node-ui) per response /basemap/ Background map: vendored style, fonts and sprites from disk, tiles proxied and cached (Basemap and external services) every app style five minutes; fonts and sprites one year /tiles/ Raster tiles via BASEMAP_PROXY only with BASEMAP_PROXY=true per upstream /ext/nominatim/, /ext/commons/, /ext/wikimedia/<host>/, /ext/mangrove/ Proxied external services (External Services) every app, unless the matching PROXY_* is false per service /legal/impressum, /legal/datenschutz Imprint and privacy notice (Legal pages); /impressum and /datenschutz redirect here every app no-store /config.js Runtime configuration, written from .env at container start every app no-store /manifest.webmanifest, /icons/ Web app manifest and its icons, for "Install app" every app no-cache; icons one day /registry.json The hub's list of data-nodes (registry.json); path set by REGISTRY_URL hubs default /federation-status.json, /metrics Health of every listed region, as JSON and for Prometheus (Hub status and metrics) real values on hubs only; a placeholder elsewhere no-store

Region URLs like /fulda are not files: the map resolves them to a place via Nominatim. A path segment named api, api2, ext, legal or metrics, or one containing a dot, is never treated as a region.

Nothing is written to an access log, on any path (Privacy by design → Nothing is written down).

docs.title: registry.json Reference
docs.text: The Hub reads a registry.json file listing the regional PostgREST backends, one entry each. Browsers load it once per page load and then refresh each listed backend's get_meta every HUB_POLL_INTERVAL (default 5 min). After editing the file, restart the hub's app container (docker compose --profile ui restart app): the Content Security Policy's connect-src is generated from it at startup, so a new backend is otherwise missing from it. The Hub fetches get_meta from each backend and, for the current view, the tier RPCs of the backends it overlaps, merges them onto a shared map, and tags every feature with its source backend so deep-links round-trip.

docs.title: Location
docs.text:
• Served from: the nginx container under /registry.json (path configurable via REGISTRY_URL).
  • Source file: app/public/registry.json in the repo. In production, replace or bind-mount with your own registry.
  • Served as: application/json. CORS is not needed for the registry file itself — the Hub fetches it from its own origin. The backends the registry points at are typically cross-origin and must enable CORS on /api/ (covered in Federation endpoints).

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
Two top-level shapes are accepted:

Object form (recommended)Bare array form (legacy) 
{
  "instances": [
    {
      "slug": "fulda",
      "url":  "https://fulda.example.org/api",
      "name": "Fulda"
    },
    {
      "slug": "mv",
      "url":  "https://mv.example.org/api",
      "name": "Mecklenburg-Vorpommern",
      "centroid": [12.43, 53.81]
    }
  ]
}

[
  { "slug": "fulda",  "url": "https://fulda.example.org/api",  "name": "Fulda"  },
  { "slug": "berlin", "url": "https://berlin.example.org/api", "name": "Berlin" }
]

Both forms are supported indefinitely. New registries should prefer the object form so future top-level metadata (e.g. a registry version) can be added without a breaking change.

docs.title: Entry fields
docs.text: Field Required Description url yes Base URL of the backend's PostgREST /api. Surrounding whitespace and trailing slashes are removed (in the browser and in the hub's health poll alike, #740). The Hub calls the tier RPCs (/rpc/get_playground_clusters, /rpc/get_playgrounds_bbox, …) and /rpc/get_meta under it. name recommended Human-readable label. Shown in the instance drawer and — until get_meta returns — used as the backend's displayed region name. Technically falls back to url if omitted, which gives ugly labels — always set it. slug no Short stable identifier used in deep-links (#<slug>/W<osm_id>). If present, features from this backend round-trip their slug back into the URL hash on selection. See validation rules below. centroid no [lon, lat] in WGS84 (e.g. [9.93, 51.54]). Sets a fallback position for the macro view ring when the backend has no bbox yet (first import not completed, or import failed). Without this field, a backend with no data is invisible on the macro view map. Once the first import completes, the bbox-derived centroid takes over automatically — no manual update needed. Note: When a backend has neither bbox nor centroid, the instance panel auto-opens to alert operators, showing a "No position set" warning with a link to troubleshooting docs. country no ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. "SK", case-insensitive). Shows a small country chip next to the name in the instance drawer, with the full country name for screen readers and as a tooltip (#741). Set it only where it tells something — on a mostly German federation, only on the non-German entries; entries without it render as before. An invalid value is ignored with a console warning.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
All three of these happened on one entry, and each one fails without an error in the hub (#740):

Mistake What you see Fix url without the /api path (https://hojdy.sk) Backend stays "unreachable" — the hub asks https://hojdy.sk/rpc/get_meta, which is a 404 End the URL with the PostgREST path, usually /api. Not repaired automatically: path-prefix deployments legitimately use other paths. Check with curl <url>/rpc/get_meta Stray whitespace or a trailing slash — Harmless since #740: both are stripped No url, or the same url twice — Skipped with a console warning naming the entry: an entry without a URL has nothing to ask, and a duplicate would never receive data, since every lookup is by URL Upper-case slug ("Kosice") Deep links fall back to the bare #W<id> form for that backend Use lower case ("kosice"). Not repaired automatically: the slug is part of links people share, so the hub must not serve a different spelling than the registry

Runtime-populated fields

The Hub does not read version or region from registry.json entries — adding those keys to the file has no effect. Both come at runtime from each backend's /api/rpc/get_meta response: the region name from the OSM relation, version from the release that last applied the backend's api.sql. The region list shows that version as a badge.

docs.title: Slug validation
docs.text:
Slugs must match ^[a-z0-9-]+$ — lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens only. Invalid slugs are logged as a console warning and treated as absent — the entry still works (playgrounds still load from that backend), but deep-links won't be slug-scoped and selections on features from that backend will fall back to the bare #W<osm_id> form.

Slugs should be stable — they are persisted in URLs shared by users. Rename with care; there's no redirect mechanism.

docs.title: Derived capabilities
docs.text: Once the registry is loaded, the Hub derives one aggregate from it:

docs.title: Aggregated bounding box
docs.text: The Hub unions every backend's get_meta().bbox into a single extent and uses it to fit the initial map view. Backends that haven't yet reported (still loading, failed, or running a version older than v0.2.1) are ignored. Until at least one backend reports a bbox, the map stays on its default Germany-wide view.

docs.title: Deep-link behaviour
docs.text:
URL hash Hub behaviour #<slug>/W<osm_id> Resolves slug → backend URL, waits for that backend's features, selects the matching osm_id. Unknown slug: logs once and retries as more backends load. #W<osm_id> Broadcast search across every loaded backend. First match wins; duplicate osm_id across backends triggers a console warning. #<anything>/W<osm_id> Standalone mode ignores the slug prefix and selects the osm_id from its sole configured backend.

When a user selects a playground, the Hub rewrites the hash to its canonical slug-scoped form if the backend has a slug, otherwise to the bare W<osm_id> form.

A standalone pitch uses P instead of W in every form (#<slug>/P<osm_id>, #P<osm_id>). A slug-less pitch link is resolved by asking every backend's get_pitch.

docs.title: See also
